📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that openAI says it made a billing mistake when it debuted its newly introduced models, GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. Its fix means paying ChatGPT consumers will hit their usage limits faster. Compared with last week, the same work will reach the limit 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol. OpenAI executive Thibault Sottiaux announced the fix on X on Thursday, as Business Insider reported.

“We made a billing mistake at launch of GPT-6.2 that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most people. We’ve fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your strategy’s usage allowance,” Sottiaux wrote.

According to recent reports, openAI will not charge customers for the difference on past usage, Sottiaux said. Both models introduced on 17 November.

“As a small token to apologize for the mistake, we’ll be adding one banked reset for everyone on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business,” he wrote.

Other models are not affected, Sottiaux said, according to Neowin. Users should still get more out of GPT-6.2 than out of GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, he added. OpenAI’s pricing pages did not change, the site added.

Reddit owners reacted with scepticism, TechRadar reported. One user called a single banked reset “pretty thin” as an apology. At launch, OpenAI had remarked both models would let users get more done within their usage limits.

It has been revealed that usage costs are a problem across the industry. Musk has said Grok Bot’s costs were unsustainably high relative to revenue, Business Insider noted.

According to recent reports, the fix lands a day after OpenAI began merging ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs for some Pro users. Under the new system, both will draw on a single usage allowance, an OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch.

Industry observers note that most users should not hit their limits more often, the spokesperson remarked. A small share of the heaviest users may. Chats with the Instant model stay unlimited and do not count towards the shared allowance. OpenAI plans to roll out shared limits more broadly in December, according to its support page.

In a recent development, openAI also gained a fresh hire from Anthropic on Wednesday. Thariq Shihipar, who left Anthropic in October, said he has joined OpenAI. He named Sottiaux and Cat Wu, Claude Code’s former product lead, among his new colleagues.

According to recent reports, I’m very proud of my time at Anthropic, and I’ll continue to root for my former colleagues. Both companies have important roles to play in the future.

There is a tremendous amount of work ahead of us to bring AI to the world, and it will demand the very best of all of us. I felt that I could personally contribute the most to this effort at OpenAI.

I believe this is one of the great strengths of Silicon Valley, the flow of ideas and people.

I’m excited to join a team I’ve long admired, building incredible AI products for over a billion people, and to work alongside friends like @_catwu, @thsottiaux, @ajambrosino, @sharifshameem, @jxnlco and many others to push the frontier forward.

More than anything, I hope to make your experience of using AI just a little bit better.

I am once again at your service.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A upcoming report indicates that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either ….

Recent findings suggest that as iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Sources indicate that some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but currently it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the company.

Industry observers note that apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand upcoming operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman claims Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

Recent findings suggest that the other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

However, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield challenges may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

1Password Security Incident

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 1password

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • Sources indicate that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our owners.
  • Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

Sources indicate that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our owners. These records include:.

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security).

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account).

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.

Industry observers note that other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers).

It has been revealed that the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning. During this incident there were a small number of consumers in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them.

The keys that protect your vaults.

1Password does not store your account password or secret key.

1Password apps and browser extensions.

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added new detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

It has been revealed that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a upcoming device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.

Sources indicate that you trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

Recent findings suggest that we are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll upgrade it if we find anything that changes what we’ve said here.

S&P puts Nvidia’s AA credit rating on downgrade watch over governance

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia’s Voyager building at its headquarters in Santa Clara, California.
  • According to recent reports, S&P Global Ratings has put Nvidia’s AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade.
  • Any cut would likely be a single notch, to AA-, S&P stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia’s Voyager building at its headquarters in Santa Clara, California.

According to recent reports, S&P Global Ratings has put Nvidia’s AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade. The Jensen Huang saga exposed weak spots in how the firm is run and overseen, the agency said in a note on Wednesday. It could cut the rating within 90 days if those problems remain.

Any cut would likely be a single notch, to AA-, S&P stated. It could go further if investigations or disclosures showed harm to Nvidia’s reputation or future business. The watch covers both the tech giant’s rating and its senior unsecured debt.

“News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in NVIDIA’s management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness,” S&P wrote.

It has been revealed that the agency said the long tenure of some directors may have compromised their independence. Nvidia’s governance may also not have kept pace with its fast growth, it added.

“While NVIDIA management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the ‘key man’ risk to the forefront,” analysts Andrew Chang and David Tsui wrote.

S&P cut its management and governance score for Nvidia to neutral from positive. Huang’s departure and his reinstatement do not answer its questions about how the board oversees executive conduct, it said. The agency plans to meet the board and management to discuss board independence, oversight and a credible succession plan.

Nvidia’s competitive position, technology lead and finances are unchanged for now, according to S&P. Stricter export controls could still slow its growth. The agency would take a harsher view if it came to believe Nvidia broke or got around export rules. The same goes for any sign that past disclosures understated its exposure to China and nearby regions.

S&P’s move follows Moody’s. On 18 November, Moody’s lowered its outlook on Nvidia to stable from positive over governance concerns, CNBC reported. Moody’s kept that outlook after Huang returned. Nvidia shares have fallen about 12.5% since Monday’s close, CNBC added.

Recent findings suggest that A lower rating could raise Nvidia’s borrowing costs. The company sold $25bn of senior notes in June, shortly after S&P raised it to AA, according to CNBC.

According to recent reports, nvidia also lends its AA rating to less creditworthy companies by backing their debt, leases and hardware purchases, Semafor reported. On Wednesday, measures of credit risk for Nvidia and CoreWeave hit record highs, Bloomberg reported, as fears over AI debt returned.

In a recent development, some critics say the agency is late. Nvidia had no board chair until Huang resigned on 12 November and Harvey Jones became its first, Martin Peers wrote in The Information. That weakness was public in Nvidia’s filings, and S&P could have flagged it earlier, he argued.

Industry observers note that apple is always iterating on the design of its software. While major overhauls like iOS 26’s Liquid Glass don’t come along often, the company makes smaller design changes all the time via software updates. In iOS 27.3, which will launch to all consumers next month, Apple has design changes coming to four popular apps: Health, Calendar, Safari, and Music.

The Health app gets the biggest design changes.

As seen above, Health introduces brand fresh Insights, Longevity, and Browse tabs that replace the previous options and include a variety of fresh UI elements like a top navigation row, personalized prompts and coaching, educational videos, and a lot more.

As the side-by-side above highlights, the buttons for search and creating a new event have moved out of the top-right corner and into the bottom of the screen.

Calendar also now shows the year at the top of the screen next to the current month, and has updated the ‘Today’ button to show the current date instead.

In a recent development, safari introduces an optional fresh design for tabs: Vertical Tabs. You can enable these inside Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Safari for a different approach to tabs across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Here’s an example of vertical tabs on iPhone Duo.

Vertical Tabs won’t be for everyone, but they’ve proven popular in other browsers, so it’s great to see Safari add the option.

Song artwork is now able to break the constraints of a square and blend seamlessly into the scrolling lyrics view. Here are examples from Beta Profiles on X:.

Terrestrial networks cannot reach every location. Oceans, remote regions, and disaster zones often remain without coverage. 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTN) address this gap by using satellites and high-altitude platforms. Introduced in 3GPP Release 17, NR-NTN keeps evolving through Releases 18, 19, and 20. Satellite links bring new challenges. Signals travel long distances, satellites move at high speed, and Doppler shift affects synchronization and timing. These effects shape payload design, mobility procedures, and device behavior. They also call for new testing methods for devices, satellites, and networks. This paper explains the technology step by step. It also shows how NTN is shaping unified terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks in 6G.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, that makes it more likely that stress in one market spreads to others, the Bank stated.
  • “Taken together, these developments heighten the risk that multiple vulnerabilities crystallise simultaneously,” the Bank’s Financial Policy Committee wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s data centre in Hamina, Finland.

It has been revealed that the Bank of England claims the way the AI boom is financed is making the global financial system more fragile. AI financing is taking a form that is “increasingly complex, circular and opaque”, the central bank warned. It set out the concern in its Financial Stability Report on Thursday.

According to recent reports, that makes it more likely that stress in one market spreads to others, the Bank stated. Higher interest rates and rising sovereign debt add to the pressure.

“Taken together, these developments heighten the risk that multiple vulnerabilities crystallise simultaneously,” the Bank’s Financial Policy Committee wrote.

It has been revealed that hyperscalers, the few tech groups that run giant data centres, are set to problem more than $305bn of bonds this year. That is around 8% of global investment-grade issuance, according to the report. Some AI companies also fund others in the sector against future revenue commitments. Such circular deals make it harder to see where risks sit, the Bank stated. The IMF raised the same worry about circular AI deals in October.

Hyperscalers now have links to the financial system of around $4tn, Bloomberg reported, citing the review. Katharine Braddick heads the Bank’s regulatory arm. She told reporters that supervisors want to stop any fall in AI values washing “back through the banking system”.

The Bank also flagged rising cyber risk. Frontier AI has kept advancing since July, especially AI agents and open-weight models, it stated. Recent incidents indicated how hard it is to stop autonomous agents acting against what developers and users intended. Open-weight models are cheaper to run and their safeguards are easier to remove, which could help attackers.

Recent Google Cloud and Microsoft outages revealed how one provider’s trouble can hit many firms at once. Further ahead, quantum computing could break widely used encryption, so a move to quantum-resistant cryptography is now a priority. The Bank is setting up a Systemic Resilience Council of industry figures and officials to coordinate its response, Bloomberg reported.

In a recent development, lenders are already shifting some of that risk. Citi and JPMorgan are marketing portfolios of AI-related loans, people familiar with the deals told Semafor. Some banks want to manage risk, while others want room to lend more.

Some deals use synthetic risk transfers. These keep the loans on a bank’s books but pass the risk of losses to investors. Banks are joining hyperscalers, which already move debt off their balance sheets, Semafor’s Ellen DiMauro wrote.

Sources indicate that the borrowing is not slowing. JPMorgan strategists expect $450bn of investment-grade AI debt next year, up from $368bn in 2026, Bloomberg reported. That comes as fears over AI debt return to markets.

The Bank still judges UK banks well capitalised and able to keep lending in a much worse downturn. It completed its review of bank capital rules on Thursday. Under the review, Tier 1 requirements for major UK banks will fall by about 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets.

“Reducing capital requirements much further would risk financial instability,” the committee added.

From the time I built a surround system from the cheapest stuff I could find on eBay to reviewing the latest and greatest sound gear, I put a whole lot of time and effort into working out which soundbars are worth your money. In a recent development, before we dive deep into the best soundbars, I just want to go through what we look for when we're testing them. We make sure to evaluate the soundbar in some key areas.

Industry observers note that setup: While it's something you're only going to do once, we want to make sure that it's as easy as possible to get working. Plug-and-play is the name of the game here, and if there are extra features we want to make sure that they're as easy as possible to use.

How big is it? Everyone's space is different. Maybe you've got a massive room with loads of stuff in it, or maybe your living room is more compact and minimal. We check whether the soundbar fits under our 50-inch OLED Philips testing TV to make sure you're not going to have any size challenges. Ultimately, it needs to fit on your TV stand.

In a recent development, are there any extras? What's in the box, and are its contents any good? Some soundbars come with extras like surround speakers and subwoofers. I want to make sure that those extras are worth it, and that they're not just pictures to sell them at the store.

According to recent reports, sound: This is arguably the most important part of the soundbar, and there are a number of things we look out for here. How's the dialog? Is it clear, or muffled? I love testing the sound portion because I get to watch movies instead of working; But it's still important when testing and working out whether a bar is for you.

But it's really that epic movie experience you're looking for with something like the Sonos Arc Ultra, and you get it in spades. The Dolby Atmos with just the soundbar is unlike anything else around, and if you add in the optional surrounds, it's a game-changer.

According to recent reports, I absolutely love watching just about anything with the Arc Ultra — although you will want to pick up a Sonos sub so that you can get the low-end grunt your movies deserve. It's not cheap — but it is so, so worth it.

There’s a subwoofer in the box that you’ll need to find space for as well.

The sound is great. It’s immersive, directional, deep and clear. We loved it when watching a wide range of movies, from action to romance. There’s little this soundbar can’t do.

Sources indicate that setupFirst off, hit the gym before you place this soundbar anywhere. This is a 26-pound behemoth, so you might even want two people to lift it into place on your TV stand. There are some extra setup quirks as well, but they’re easily mitigated thanks to the good instructions and user-friendly design.

Recent findings suggest that once you’ve plugged the soundbar and subwoofer into the wall, you’ll hook the soundbar into the eARC port of your TV. The soundbar and sub should find each other automatically, but if not, use the connection button on the sub.

If you want to use the surrounds, pull them off the soundbar and place them around your room. Sound adjustment is done automatically. If you have any wireless connection issues, re-attach them to the soundbar to reset everything.

In a recent development, streaming and Wi-Fi are handled by JBL’s ONE app. It’s super easy; we had no problems at all getting everything connected and working.

In a recent development, how big is itThere’s no two ways around it — the 1300XMK2 is a very big soundbar. At 40 inches, the soundbar is wide, and that's without taking extra surrounds into account. It’s very deep too, so you’ll want to make sure that there’s enough space on your TV stand that way. If not, we’d recommend wall mounting the TV.

Recent findings suggest that this is a bar suited to much larger TVs, 65-inch at a minimum. Otherwise you’ll risk the bar looking too big, and your TV small.

According to recent reports, thankfully, you won’t have to worry about how tall the bar is. It’s short enough that most TVs will amply clear the top, so you don’t have to worry about the soundbar blocking the view. Just bear in mind that you’ll also want space for the surround speakers behind your seating position — they’re not going to work if they’re in front of you.

Recent findings suggest that are there any extrasYou get everything you need in the box. There’s the bar itself, along with the surround speakers. Unlike other models, from the likes of Sonos, this is a substantial bonus and means you don’t have to buy any further devices for some lovely Dolby Atmos sound.

According to recent reports, there’s also a subwoofer in the box, along with all the cables you’d ever need for just about any circumstance. There’s a controller in the box, although we found that the JBL ONE app was a perfectly serviceable way of controlling the sound — or your TV remote through the eARC port.

It has been revealed that soundWith 23 drivers powering 11.1.4 channels, you’d hope the 1300XMK2 sounded good. And, sure enough, the bar sounds excellent. Those extra surrounds make sure that the sound is immersive and massive, while the sub adds impressive depth and bass.

The planes flying in Top Gun: Maverick made the room shake, and the soundtrack was bombastic during testing. The whole movie placed our tester directly in the movie.

Object placement is good too, making sure that everything is kept in the right place.

The soundbar was pretty good for music too, making soundtracks sound great, although it struggled slightly more with stereo tracks — but it's still better than most soundbars.

Industry observers note that want everything in one box but don't want to spend every single dollar you have? The QS750F is a great option, with extra surround speakers and a subwoofer for less than $1000.

According to recent reports, soundbars are expensive — there’s no way around that. You want to achieve the best bang-for-buck sound, right? Enter the Samsung QS750F. For a relatively low MSRP of $899, the QS750F gives you a soundbar, two rears, and a subwoofer, which is considerably more generous than Sonos or JBL.

As a result, the QS750F blows the competition out of the park. For under $1k, you get cinematic sound, with enviable width and immense bass. The QS750F sounds so good that we forgot we were supposed to be reviewing it.

Although it’s just a 5.1.2 channel configuration — considerably fewer speakers than JBL’s monstrous 1300XMK2, which boasts 11.1.4 channels and costs almost double — you probably wouldn’t be able to notice the difference.

Industry observers note that setupAs with every other soundbar, setup is a relatively quick process. Once the soundbar, subwoofer, and rears are unpackaged, simply connect everything to power and plug the soundbar into your TV using HDMI eARC.

Industry observers note that unlike JBL’s collection of premium soundbars, the QS750F’s rears aren’t truly “wireless” — sure, they connect to the soundbar wirelessly, but the left speaker must be connected to power. This is only an concern if you’re short on power outlets, extension cables, or if you want a particularly cable-free setup. Even so, you’re not going to get a better multi-speaker setup for less, so we think this is a worthy sacrifice.

Sources indicate that the subwoofer is wireless, so don’t worry about needing to connect that to the soundbar with a wire. It’ll automatically connect.

It has been revealed that how major is itAs you might expect, the QS750F is a large soundbar. This is true of pretty much every high-power soundbar — they’re designed to be able to fill large rooms with both size and physical presence.

Recent findings suggest that the soundbar is 46 inches long and ten inches deep, so you’ll need to ensure it fits on your TV stand/wall mount and that your TV is big enough. I’d recommend anything from 55 inches up.

The subwoofer is effectively a 10 x 10 x 10-inch cube. We’d recommend positioning the subwoofer around 12 inches from the walls on all sides. You’ll need to play around with spacing to figure out the optimal position. Some setups come with configuration modes in the relevant app, but Samsung locks its proprietary Space Fit Pro behind post-2021 AI-powered Samsung TVs.

Are there any extrasThe QS750F comes with everything you need for a Dolby Atmos all-in-one setup. You get the soundbar, subwoofer, and two rears.

Recent findings suggest that you also get AirPlay, Google Cast, and smart home features in the SmartThings app, which we’d recommend downloading. You can easily adjust playback modes and listening styles — movie, music, gaming, voice enhancement — to find what pleases you.

In a recent development, soundAlright, now onto the most important part of any soundbar: its audio output. Thankfully, you’ll be pleased to know that the QS750F sounds utterly fantastic.

Recent findings suggest that as the QS750F is a large soundbar, it’s intended for use in a large room. The side-firing speakers in the soundbar itself and the powerful subwoofer work together to create a wide soundscape worthy of a movie theater. Although there’s not as much height as width, the soundbar’s Dolby Atmos performance is still admirable.

In a recent development, the dialogue performance is a clear standout, though: I was never left wondering what was being mentioned thanks to voice enhancement mode. This feature isolated dialogue well, and ensured even the moodiest and broodiest speech was crystal clear.

It has been revealed that most audiophiles will be the first to admit that soundbars aren’t ideal for playing music — me included — but the QS750F didn’t balk at the challenge. Although I’d much rather listen to music via my bookshelf speakers or headphones, the QS750F played every song with rich, pulsing bass, and would be good enough for a quick listening session or party.

It has been revealed that sonos' compact soundbar brings excellent sound with a slightly higher price tag than the old model — but the app is still a bit tetchy. Still, this great-sounding bar is a great option for Sonos homes with living rooms too small for the Arc Ultra.

The Sonos Beam Ultra feels like a statement of intent. The app works better than ever, the sound is incredible, and the surround sound straight out of the bar itself is top-notch. There are still problems — music sounds bad, and a lack of HDMI passthrough is a shame.

According to recent reports, but this is Sonos on top form. The design is great, bringing that Sonos minimalism to a smaller bar than the enormous Arc Ultra. It’s perhaps a little more plain than some of the brand's other devices, but it's a handsome thing that’ll blend in perfectly with any living room decor. The traditional black and white colorways are still the only options, unfortunately.

Recent findings suggest that and then there’s the way it sounds. It increases the Dolby Atmos effect with height channels, making for a more immersive movie experience that lands you directly in the center of the action. Add in a few extra Sonos speakers for a full surround setup and you have the perfect movie-watching experience for a smaller space.

It is expensive, mind you. The Beam was never cheap, but this one ups the price ante to make it a less compelling buy than other bars around this size class. And while Sonos app is much better than it was in early 2025, I’ve had more problems with it than our tester, with dropouts and other problems.

According to recent reports, setup is super easy. You just plug the soundbar into a wall outlet, and then an HDMI cable into the eARC port on the back of your TV. That could be it, if you’re not interested in any of the extra Sonos features.

Sources indicate that to finish setup you’ll need to use the Sonos app, which is now much improved. From there you can do sound tuning setup amongst other things, like connecting extra Sonos surround speakers or a subwoofer for extra bass. It’s simple and easy to do, and the app will take you through it step by step.

This is also where you’ll stream audio to the device or adjust any settings. There’s no remote that comes with the soundbar — everything goes through the Sonos app.

The Beam Ultra really stretches the “compact” soundbar thing. It measures around 30 inches wide, making it a larger soundbar than some of the smaller compact options. That makes it perfect for TVs around 55 inches and smaller, though Sonos says it works for TVs up to 65 inches.

For larger spaces and TVs you’ll want the larger Sonos Arc Ultra.

Industry observers note that in the box, you’ll find the soundbar, a power cable, and the HDMI cable. That’s it. There’s no remote, no wall mount — just the soundbar.

It has been revealed that you can buy extras. Sonos speakers, the Era 100, 300, Sub Mini and Sub 4 all work as surround options for the Beam Ultra. I’d recommend the Era 100 and Sub Mini for smaller rooms if you want to increase the surround capability of the bar.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, everything has to come from Sonos’ rather enclosed ecosystem. You cannot add a separate 3rd-party subwoofer, for example. Shame.

The Beam Ultra is the best Dolby Atmos soundbar for its size. There’s real height to the sound here, making for a far better immersive bubble than other similarly sized bars. There’s width too — it’s a great way to watch your favorite movies.

Unfortunately, stereo music sounds straight up bad. That’s a shame, given that Sonos nailed it with the Arc Ultra — if you want to listen to music, you’re better off grabbing a stereo pair of Era 100s. It’ll cost you less, too.

I've seen loads of soundbars pass over Tom's Guide's testing table, and while there are some excellent options out there, not all of them can fit onto one list.

That doesn't mean they're bad, by any stretch, and they might just be the best soundbar for you. Here are some of the soundbars that we liked testing but didn't quite make the cut for the main roundup.

For the same money as Sonos's Beam Ultra, the Marshall Heston 60 is another compelling compact option. It might not quite reach the same heady heights as the Beam Ultra for movie watching, but it absolutely obliterates the Sonos when it comes to listening to music. It's just a shame that there aren't any surround speaker options.

Read our full Marshall Heston 60 review.

Recent findings suggest that samsung's biggest and most premium sound is very good, offering excellent Dolby Atmos out of the box thanks to its included subwoofer and surround speakers. If you're looking for an all-in-one package for a Samsung TV it's a great option, but we believe the JBL equivalent offers a more rounded surround experience. If you're looking for the best soundbar surround sound, then look for the more expensive Sonos setup.

Read our full Samsung Q990H review.

This mid-range soundbar brings excellent sound, but it forgot to bring the premium price. You won't get any smart features, which is a shame, but when it sounds this good, you won't really care. The sub in the box is surprisingly strong for this price point, and the bar itself offers solid surround for the dollars you'll pay.

Read our full Samsung Q600F review.

Sources indicate that the KEF XIO is one of the best-sounding soundbars we've ever tested. It's also one of the best-looking and best-built. "So why isn't it on the list!?" Because it costs $2,500. While I let that sink in for a second, I'll also tell you that the app experience is hit or miss. Still, if you have the dollars lying around, there are far worse ways to spend thousands of smackeroos.

LG's Sound Suite Dolby Atmos FlexConnect (phew) technology is very cool, and in the right room it can sound very good. Unfortunately, its core sound simply isn't up to scratch when compared to the competition, and the Sound Suite FlexConnect speakers are sold separately for a hefty premium. A proof of concept that demonstrates its worth waiting for the sequel — but it needs some more time in the oven.

Read our full Sound Suite H7 review.

The Polk Audio Signa S4 brings a great sound and surprisingly solid Dolby Atmos for a decent price. The included sub is plenty bassy, and there's good spaciousness to the sound. It's a large bar despite its lower price. The comprehensive remote control is comfortable and easy to use.

Read our full Polk Audio Signa S4 review.

If you want something that looks super sleek and tidy, then the True X Bar is a great option. Its Dolby Atmos performance is admirable, and the price is right. We reviewed the 40A, but you can find the 50A for around the same price now. It's exactly the same, but comes with a subwoofer. But you can also buy the 40A and add a subwoofer later.

Read our full Yamaha True X Bar 40A review.

One of the best bits of most modern soundbars is that they're all simple to use in some form or another — but if you want something that you just plug in and use, then you'll want to avoid any with smart features.

Industry observers note that while those smart features can make them sound better, or work for different types of content, they add complexity. An app might make it possible to access room EQs and the like, it also makes it more complicated for the end user.

Sources indicate that although we used to recommend avoiding Wi-Fi connections and apps if you just want to plug in and play, almost all soundbars now have some smart features. So I'd recommend looking for models that don't solely rely on those if the physical connection is your main focus.

Recent findings suggest that first up, if your primary use case is music, go for a pair of speakers with an HDMI port like the Fluance Ri71. They sound much better than soundbars for music. You'll thank me later.

In a recent development, now, for the other questions. TV users will want something that increases dialoge clarity and makes it easier to hear what's going on in the news. You won't need a subwoofer or any kind of surround support. The Sony HT-S100F above is going to be perfect for you, given it's not too expensive and works great for TV.

Recent findings suggest that movie watchers should look out for subwoofers and surround speakers. You want more space for your Dolby Atmos mixes and the subwoofer will help with the low-end rumble you get with movies. The Sonos Arc Ultra and subwoofer is a good option for you, or the JBL Bar 1300XMK2 if you want something in one package.

Industry observers note that if you have a small room or use a small TV, you don't want a massive soundbar; that much should be obvious. It wouldn't fit, for one, but it would also make your TV look much smaller. And who wants that.

In a recent development, however, you also don't want a soundbar that's too small for your TV. Otherwise, all of the sound will appear to come from the middle of the TV, rather than from it's sides like it should.

You'll want to get a decently sized soundbar if you've got something between 50-75 inches significant. Larger than that and you should probably consider either the biggest soundbar you can lay your hands on, or a proper stereo setup built around one of the best home cinema receivers.

WhatsApp starts rolling out scheduled messages to users worldwide

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that whatsApp has started rolling out scheduled messages, which let users write a message now and have it sent automatically at a later date and time.
  • To schedule a message, users press and hold the send button in a chat and choose a date and time.
  • Owners can schedule text, photos and videos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that whatsApp has started rolling out scheduled messages, which let users write a message now and have it sent automatically at a later date and time. The Meta-owned app announced the feature on 25 November and calls it one of its most-requested features.

To schedule a message, users press and hold the send button in a chat and choose a date and time. Messages can be set between 10 minutes and 14 days ahead, and the feature works in both one-to-one and group chats.

Owners can schedule text, photos and videos. Pending messages can be viewed and deleted at any point before they go out, and they arrive looking like any other message.

Scheduled messages are still end-to-end encrypted, so WhatsApp cannot read them. They also send at the chosen time even if the sender’s phone is switched off or its battery has run out.

According to recent reports, the feature is reaching users globally over the coming weeks. WhatsApp did not say whether it will reach Android, iPhone and the desktop apps at the same time.

It has been revealed that the launch follows months of testing. WABetaInfo, which tracks WhatsApp test builds, first spotted the feature in development in February. It reached a small group of Android beta testers in October, before arriving for some iPhone testers.

Industry observers note that during testing, scheduled messages were kept in a dedicated section of each chat’s info screen, WABetaInfo reported. Testers could attach only one photo or video per scheduled message, and recipients were not told that a message had been scheduled. Deleting one before it went out did not notify them either.

Rival messaging apps have offered similar tools for some time. Telegram already lets owners schedule messages, and Apple has offered a Send Later option in its Messages app since iOS 18. Google Messages also supports scheduled texts.

Recent findings suggest that until now, WhatsApp customers who wanted to send a message later had to rely on reminders or third-party tools. Businesses that use the app to take orders from retailers have also built their own workarounds on top of it.

The app passed three billion monthly users in 2025, according to Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg. India and Brazil are its largest markets, by number of users.

When you're pumping weights or running a marathon, you're going to want something to keep your mind occupied — and there's little better than the best workout headphones. Listen to music, catch up with your favorite podcast, or devour some of an audiobook. Whatever you're doing you'll need some buds.

It has been revealed that there are loads of options out there, but some are better than others. Our favorites are the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2, with their great sound perfectly pairing with solid ANC and a comfortable fit.

Sources indicate that we've tested plenty more of course, and we've tested as many as we can. So read on to find out which headphones you should be getting for your next sweat-proof listening session.

AI seems to be the latest fitness trend, popping up in smartwatches, workout apps, and headphones. I wouldn't recommend picking up a newly introduced pair of earbuds for these features. My experience is the AI functions aren't very useful, and will likely change a lot in the next few years. So, focus on finding a set that feel and sound good, allowing you to focus on your exercise without distraction.

Sources indicate that for a long time, Beats headphones didn't make me think of exercise. But that was before Apple redesigned the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 in early 2025 into what are effectively AirPods for workouts, with active noise cancellation (ANC), an effective transparency mode, and proper support for iPhone and Android devices.

Industry observers note that the winged design of the older Powerbeats Pro has been replaced with over-ear hooks, which are a lot more stable. I'd sometimes need to fiddle a bit to get them on, but once locked into place, they didn't budge. And because the hook keeps some of the weight out of your ear, they were comfortable to wear for hours at a time.

Though the downside of this design is that the case is pretty big, and much larger than you'd comfortably fit into leggings or a pocket; fine for throwing in a gym bag, less ideal for carrying about, unlike the minuscule Beats Solo Buds case. But this one tops the battery up to 45 hours, while the Solo Buds case is just for storage.

The Powerbeats Pro 2 come with Apple's H2 chip, just like the AirPods Pro 3, so expect similar speedy performance, although I didn't find the noise cancellation or transparency mode were quite up to the flagship buds' standard. Though I did jump with delight at the use of physical buttons on each bud.

In a recent development, these headphones powered me through weights workouts, meditation sessions and long outdoor walks with no issues. I put them in and they did exactly what I wanted; good audio with no fuss. I don't run, but my coworker Nick Harris-Fry does, and found the Powerbeats Pro 2 a good companion for runs too.

It has been revealed that the company leaned heavily into the buds' heart rate monitor at launch. It's neat, but you'll probably never use it. There's a small optical sensor built into the buds which is used to track your heart rate during workouts, but if this is something you care about, you likely have a smartwatch or Garmin watch that can do this better.

If you’re looking for some top-notch earbuds for working out that won’t break the bank, then look no further than the CMF By Nothing Buds 2. With loads of gym-centric features at a price that’s less than a fifth of some of the more expensive options on the list, they’re a fantastic way to keep fit while listening to tunes. Or a podcast. Or like, white noise. Whatever floats your workout boat.

At this price point, you wouldn’t expect to find anything with noise canceling, let alone ANC that works this well. It did a great job of keeping a noisy office at bay, so the pounding techno in the gym will be no problem. Outdoor runners, rejoice, they also blocked out traffic sounds when our tester, Ashley, took them out for a walk.

It has been revealed that you don’t have to worry about your sweaty ears destroying them either, thanks to IP55 water resistance. You won’t be able to wear them while swimming, but anything you might get up to around your block or at the gym is no problem at all. Music, come rain or shine.

Industry observers note that you don’t even have to worry about them running out of juice mid-workout. The quoted battery life from CMF is 12 hours — we found that around 5 hours of use left us with 60% remaining. Add in the 55 hours in the case, and you’re home free for super lengthy sessions.

They’re a little cheap-looking and the environmental noise canceling in calls is… not great. But then you look at your bank balance, realize that choosing the cheaper earbuds has left you with spare cash for a better gym subscription, and suddenly everything seems to make sense again.

According to recent reports, they go in your ears, stay there, and play music while you get on with your workout. Better yet, they’ve done it for less than just about anything else around. What more could you want?

The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 are the follow-up to our former favorite running headphones, the OpenRun Pro. These bone conduction headphones sound great, despite the fact they use vibrations on your cheeks to transmit audio.

While out running with the OpenRun Pro 2 (or most Shokz headphones for that matter), we found that the fit was comfortable and secure, so you won't need to continually fiddle with them and can focus on your training.

According to recent reports, the downside to the headband-style design is that you can't adjust the fit. However, there's a smaller edition (OpenRun Pro 2 Mini) that has a shorter band for improved fit. But we were impressed with the comfort during runs, bike rides, and yoga sessions.

You don't get a charging case, but we found that the battery would last around 12 hours between top-ups, which should see you through most workouts. That noted, if you like to dial up the volume to max, expect closer to 10 hours of power.

According to recent reports, I'm not a runner, but my multi-marathoner coworker Nick Harris-Fry summed up his feelings on the headphones, concluding: "They’re my preferred running headphones at the moment because of the excellent fit, open design and good sound. If you just want running headphones with an open design, it’s the OpenRun Pro 2.".

They can survive sweaty workouts and light rain, but if you plan to train in the wet or want a more multi-functional set that'll cope with a dip in the pool, the OpenSwim Pro are a good alternative, and they have onboard MP3 storage.

It has been revealed that the AirPods Pro 3 are Apple's newest flagship headphones, and stuffed with more features than ever. There's live translation, voice isolation on calls and head gestures to control your phone. All of that's great, but it's the fitness features that really stand out.

Like the Powerbeats Pro 2, the AirPods Pro 3 now have built-in heart rate sensors. Unlike the Beats set at launch, you can actually use the sensors with a load of different apps, including (importantly) Apple Fitness.

The upcoming integration with Apple Fitness adds Workout Buddy, an AI-powered 'coach' which sends you motivational messages and performance stats, like an audio-only version of what you'd find on the Apple Watch Series 12.

I'm generally skeptical about features like this, but our resident marathon runner, Nick Harris-Fry, actually seemed impressed with the heart rate accuracy, which informs a lot of the performance metrics on Workout Buddy and Apple Fitness.

Recent findings suggest that then there's the fit. Despite being popular workout earbuds, I've always found that AirPods need quite a lot of fiddling to keep them in place. But that's not the case with the redesigned tip here, which Fitness Editor Jane McGuire said performed brilliantly on runs.

Despite being one of the first mainstream brands to launch water-resistant phones, the AirPods Pro 2 were surprisingly vulnerable, with just an IPX4 rating, essentially for splashes. The Pro 3 upgrade to a much hardier IP57 for dust and water resistance, so you can finally use them in the elements.

Like the AirPods Pro 2 before, the Pro 3 are still disappointing on the battery front; eight hours per bud, up to 24 hours with the case (while you got 30 out of the case on the Pro 2). It's not terrible, but the sub-$50 JLab Go Air Pop also reach 8 hours.

It has been revealed that the main reason I don't rate these higher in the list of best workout headphones is mostly due to the design — these aren't made for sports and they're not as secure a fit as you'd need for all high-intensity workouts. But for general use with your iPhone, including yoga, HIIT sessions, and casual runs, they're a great choice.

As Google continues to develop the Pixel-branded ecosystem of devices to rival Apple's iPhone and AirPods, it's no surprise that the Google Pixel Buds Pro 2 are the best workout headphones for Android, even if they are targeted squarely at owners of the brand's range of Pixel phones.

The key upgrade from the first-generation Pixel Buds Pro is the addition of Google Gemini, the brand's generative AI model. As it's still fairly new, it doesn't replace the older virtual Google Assistant, although in theory it can. But in practice, we found that it doesn't always offer the most accurate answers.

In a recent development, features like voice assistants and hands-free controls are useful, but not essential when you're working out. Instead, it's more key that they stay in place as you exercise. The Pixel Buds Pro 2 have a fresh wing on each bud to help them lock into your ears.

In a recent development, this would be great, but it doesn't quite reach the inner-top part of your ear, so we still found a bit of adjustment was needed to keep them in position for optimal noise cancellation. Google also claims to have improved the ANC, but it's hard to really tell the difference between the Pixel Buds Pro 2 and the original.

However, it's still effective, blocking out most noises except for some higher frequency sounds like crying babies and emergency service sirens. The sound quality matches the Pixel Buds Pro, although you may want to tweak the EQ to your preferences, as the default setting is a bit heavy on the lower end.

Sources indicate that one other thing they have in common with the AirPods Pro is that they're not necessarily the best workout headphones if you spend hours training every week, as the fit isn't quite optimized for high-impact exercise. But if you're after a versatile option to wear at the gym and at the office, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 are a great choice.

According to recent reports, bone conduction headphones are cool, but they’re bulky. Your common earbuds sound great, but they have a habit of making it difficult to hear your surroundings. Open earbuds, like the Beyerdynamic Amiron Zero, are a great middle ground that offer solid sound while allowing you to hear the rogue bus that’s bearing down on you as you do your morning run.

Sources indicate that they’re surprisingly secure, their silicone “hinges” holding onto your outer ear with little discomfort and no wiggle. Ashley, our tester, had no problem wearing them for hours and hours on end, partly thanks to their lightweight design. Just remember that these are completely open, playing the sound at your ears rather than in. Everyone is going to hear your playlist. Everyone.

Industry observers note that the battery life could be better. There are 20 hours total on tap here, which falls down compared to in-ear options. You’ll be reaching for the charging cable more often than not, unfortunately, although you won’t need to pop them in the charging case as often with 6 hours of realistic listening time. Our tests pretty much confirmed this number.

Sound-wise, these are a great alternative to in-ear buds. There’s less bass than we might like overall, but there’s little else we’d ask for. The mids sound good, and the treble is solid as well. Don’t expect game-changing audio, but for open buds these sound great.

Even better, you can change the EQ. That’s a major bonus for something like this, and it means you can change the sound to your heart's content so that they sound great no matter your sonic preference. Five bands of adjustment, baby.

Sources indicate that they’re IP54 water- and dust-resistant too, so you don’t have to worry about your sweaty ears causing any problems down the line. These are a good pair of earbuds that open you up to safer, more aware exercise — we really like them.

Recent findings suggest that the workout headphones in the guide above aren't the only ones we've tested. We regularly try out workout earbuds so that we can recommend the top options that are worth spending your hard-earned cash on.

It has been revealed that however, there are several other good options if you're after a bit more choice. These are the earbuds we've tested that didn't quite make the cut.

Industry observers note that I really, really like these headphones. They're almost the perfect version of Beats' workout headphones, but the fit (ahem) isn't always perfect, and when they're only $50 less than the much more stable Powerbeats Pro 2 with fewer features and worse battery life, you're better off with the Pro 2.

Read our full Beats Powerbeats Fit review.

In a recent development, the OpenFit Air 2 are great open earbuds, featuring solid sound and a comfortable fit. What holds them back from a full mention on the list is the fiddli-ness of the ear hooks — the clip-on design is superior if you're looking for something both secure and easy to wear.

Read our full Shokz OpenFit Air 2 review.

When Apple rolled out these in mid-2024, I loved them, even though they didn't have noise cancellation or a charging case. But now these are only marginally cheaper than the much better Powerbeats Fit, and about the same price as the more feature-packed JLab Go Air Pop, it's hard to recommend them.

Read our full Beats Solo Buds review.

The JBL SoundGear Sense have an open-ear design, so they sit on top of your ears rather than in them. We found this was fine for quiet environments or working out at home, but as soon as there was a lot of background noise from wind or traffic, it'd easily drown out the audio. They're comfortable and durable, but best-suited to indoor exercise.

Read our full JBL SoundGear Sense review.

Before investing your money in a set of workout headphones, you want to be sure that they do what they claim and are comfortable enough to wear during your training. That's why we put each set to the test before including it in the guide.

It has been revealed that I've been testing headphones for almost ten years and know the most key areas to check out before recommending any pair. You really don't want them to fall out and get lost or need to continually adjust them in your ears.

So, we wear the headphones across a range of training styles, including high-impact runs (which can cause a lot of vibration and movement), intense fast-paced workouts and weightlifting sessions to see how they fare.

If they easily stay in place, they glide through this test, but it's not a write-off if they do move — headphones that struggle with runs may still make great weights companions — so we move into other areas, like comfort and sound.

For longer sessions, including runs, yoga classes and extended gym sessions, we check that the headphones are actually comfortable in your ears and don't leave you with ear pain or pressure headaches, which can happen with some sets.

Likewise, you don't want them to run out of battery mid-session, so we check how the battery life stacks up to the manufacturer's specs. For earbuds, we see how long they last out of the case and confirm how long the case can boost that.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to sound quality, even the best workout headphones aren't going to be a match for the best audiophile headphones in terms of clarity and detail. But that doesn't mean you need to put up with poor or low-quality audio.

We use a consistent playlist of music to help compare the headphones to other sets we've tested, which includes a variety of motivational dance music, dynamic rock songs, and everything in between, including the best upcoming workout music.

Industry observers note that there are a lot of Bluetooth workout headphones out there, so it can be a challenge to decide between them all. However, there are a few considerations to keep in mind that'll help narrow your options down to the right ones for your needs.

Firstly, it's vital that they stay in place during your exercise sessions. Some have ear hooks to physically hold them down, but others rely on clever engineering, a range of ear tips, or a specific set of materials to stop them falling out.

You also want them to survive some degree of moisture. If you proposal to get sweaty, then you'll need a set rated to at least IPX4 for water resistance. But for outdoor workouts with a chance of rain, it's best to aim for an IPX7 rating.

Sources indicate that importantly, they also need to last the length of your workout. If you're doing short, high-intensity sessions, then you may only need an hour of battery. But with the right case, you may only need to recharge them every couple of weeks.

If long runs are more your thing or you're training for a marathon, you'll need a long-lasting set, like the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, which are specifically designed with long distance outdoor runners in mind and last up to 12 hours.

Sources indicate that and, finally, how loud do you like your workouts? If you don't mind some background noise at the gym, then a set of passive noise-canceling headphones should do the job, but most of the best workout earbuds have active noise cancellation (ANC) instead.

Industry observers note that earbuds with ANC cancel out the sound before it even hits your ears, so they're ideal if you want to zone out to your favorite tracks and focus on your exercise. But you may also want to hear traffic when you're out and about, so choose a set with a transparency mode too, which cancels most, but not all, noise.

In mid-2025, I had to do something hard; say goodbye to the Jabra Elite 8 Active. These were my favorite workout earbuds, but Jabra decided to focus only on business audio and no longer makes consumer earbuds or headphones.

I'd been using Jabra's Elite Active headphones since 2019, and for more than half a decade they comfortably sat atop my list of the best workout headphones. But we move. Times have changed, and they're gone (but still supported, for now).

You'd struggle to find a new pair now as most retailers have run down their supplies, but if you're after new workout earbuds, and to my mind, the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 are a worthy successor (even if they do add an ear hook).

If you've been hunting for new workout headphones, you may have noticed that each set has an IP rating for water resistance. This stands for Ingress Protection, and it's a measure of how well the buds can stand dirt and water.

There's a standard format to the rating — IPXY — where X refers to the level of dust protection and Y relates to the device's water resistance. The dust protection runs from 0 to 6, while water ranges between 0 and 9.

In a recent development, unless you're working out in very dusty environments, the dust protection is less relevant and most brands don't even test them against that part of the standard. Instead, you'll want to pay attention to the water rating.

According to recent reports, headphones with an IPX4 rating are protected against water, so will cope with sweaty workouts. However, if you want to run in the rain (or are worried about getting caught in a storm) then aim for a set with an IPX7 rating.

Industry observers note that this means they can be submerged in water up to 1 meter deep for 30 minutes without damage. That doesn't mean you should take them swimming (you'll want some waterproof headphones for that) but dropping them in a puddle isn't going to do them any harm.

In a recent development, our roundup only includes workout earbuds, but it's not uncommon to see some people train with over-ear headphones instead, especially at the gym. So, which should you wear for exercise?

Ultimately, it comes down to preference, but there are a few factors to consider. Over-ears use an adjustable headband to keep them in place, so they're not likely to move about, especially if you're lifting weights.

Even just a few years ago, in-ear buds weren't really designed with exercise in mind, so they'd often fall out or need a lot of fiddling to keep them in place. But the best workout headphones we've included here all have ways to overcome that challenge.

Some, like the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2, have ear hooks to hold them securely, while others use a combination of weight balance and grippy materials to prevent them falling from your ear mid-workout.

But many people also feel like a larger set of headphones will have longer battery life and sound better too. However, the performance gap has shrunk, so you can get impressive noise cancellation and battery life from workout earbuds now.

The downside to over-ears is that they're generally not designed for sweaty exercise. Many have leather ear pads, and these quickly wear with repeated movements and contact with sweat. You can replace them, but it's not ideal.

The earbuds are also lighter, so you're less likely to notice you have them in, while over-ear cans can start to press against your skull and contribute to tension headaches, unless they're specifically designed for comfort. Although that usually makes them less durable.

It has been revealed that generally, no. This is partly due to the intricate designs required to make small earbuds packed with batteries, sensors, and headphone components. But it's also because most brands don't prioritize repairability.

Many sets, like those in our best workout headphones roundup, are durable, so shouldn't get easily damaged. And since most offer some degree of water resistance, a bit of sweat or light rain shouldn't cause you any problems.

Sources indicate that so any significant damage is going to come from accidents, like dropping a weight onto an errant bud. However, you may notice a drop in battery life in the longer term, which you usually can't do anything about.

The only way around this would be to pick up a set of the Fairphone Fairbuds 2, which may be the world's most repairable earbuds since you can replace seven parts, including the battery and outer shell.

Sources indicate that all of the sets in our best workout headphones roundup are wireless and connect to your smartphone or other devices via Bluetooth. But you can still find wired sets, including the Apple EarPods, which look a bit like AirPods but with a cable and Lightning connector to plug into your iPhone.

Wired sets also tend to be cheaper, so you may be considering a set that you wouldn't need to worry as much about damaging or replacing. However, it's important to consider how you like to train before picking up a wired set.

It has been revealed that to keep them connected, you'll need to have your phone somewhere on your body, either in a pocket, waistband or running phone holder. Consequently, there are two different devices moving at different times as you exercise; your earphones and your smartphone.

The movements are translated between them with the cable, so if you stretch your leg out, the cable tenses and may tug on your earphones, which could lead to them falling out.

Plus, if you're working out with weights or other equipment, there's also the risk that the wire will get tangled up, leading to the headphones falling out or the cable getting ripped.

Industry observers note that similarly, if you prefer to keep aware of your surroundings, you can use most wireless workout headphones in mono mode, with just a single earbud in while the other stays in the case. You don't have the same option for wired workout headphones.

Many runners would advise picking up a set of the best bone conduction headphones for running. Like the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 in our roundup, these use vibrating pads on your cheekbones to reproduce audio, leaving your ears free to pick up the sounds around you, like traffic and other people.

This is very helpful while out running, especially if you want to run safely in the dark. Although music can be a great motivator, you don't want to miss crucial alerts like emergency vehicle sirens or bikes coming up behind you.

Recent findings suggest that plus, it means that you're more aware of everything else going on around you, including other runners and pedestrians. And if you plan to run races, using bone conduction headphones allows you to chat with other runners and listen to music.

You can get similar effects with most of the best workout headphones, as transparency modes use the earbuds' built-in mics to elevate environmental noise, but bone conduction headphones also wrap around your head, so stay in place more effectively during high-impact activities like running.

If you want to prevent your earbuds falling out of your ears or slipping out of place, the first thing to consider if the type of exercise you want to do. For running and other high-impact activities like jumping, the most secure type of workout headphones are those with ear hooks.

It has been revealed that these sit above your ear to prevent them moving or falling out, and so can cope more effectively with vibrations. This is also why many runners opt for a set of the best bone conduction headphones, since these wrap around your head to similar effect.

If you want more minimalist earbuds, then before you start your workout, you can adjust the silicone ear tips. Most sets come with a small, medium, and large replacement pair of tips so you can find the ones that fit your ear size the most.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.
  • It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.
  • It has been revealed that identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.

It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.

It has been revealed that identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors. A panel of low-vision and legally blind developers provided feedback at each stage of design.

It has been revealed that intel One Mono also covers a wide range of over 200 languages using the Latin script. The Intel One Mono fonts are provided in four weights — Light, Regular, Medium, and Bold — with matching italics, and we are happy to share both an official release of fonts ready to use as well as editable sources.

In a recent development, to install the fonts, please use the provided builds under Releases. Please refer to your software’s documentation for how to activate and use these fonts.

We recommend using these fonts at 7 points and larger in print, 9 pixels and larger on screen. The .ttf, .woff and .woff2 fonts provided in the official release have been manually optimized for screen display, improving clarity and legibility, especially on Windows platforms.

Outside of the default characters, there are a few extra features that are accessible in some applications, as well as via CSS:.

Programming ligatures are not active by default. To use them, activate the stylistic sets of your preference in your code editor. For example:.

You will find editable sources in the sources directory. The instances subfolder contains separate source files for each style of the typeface. Sources are provided in .ufo files, which contain complete artwork, links to OpenType features provided in separate .fea files, as well as meta information like naming and vertical alignments for each style of the typeface.

In a recent development, these are not installable fonts, but rather the source files that produce them: UFO (Unified Font Object) is an open, human-readable font source file format; you can find the file spec here. These sources were created using RoboFont. Many other font editors will also be able to open .ufo files; we recommend using RoboFont version 4.4.

In a recent development, for instances, you will find postscript and truetype subfolders; these contain separate source files for the .otf format and the .ttf/.woff/.woff2 files respectively. Since the format for the outline drawings differs between these sets of formats, for best results we recommend using the postscript sources to create .otf fonts, and the TrueType sources to create .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 fonts.

After making your desired edits, you can generate installable fonts directly from the font editor using its “Generate Font” functionality. If you use RoboFont, any install options should default to the ideal settings, but here they are for reference:.

Recent findings suggest that if you would like to apply edits across multiple weights, a more advanced yet potentially efficient way is to edit the masters. These are special sources that describe the extreme points in the design space — the lightest and heaviest weights for both roman and italic designs.

According to recent reports, after editing masters, you will need to rerun interpolation to generate individual weights and styles within that design space. This requires the .designspace files enclosed with the masters. The designspace format is an open, XML-based format that describes interpolation spaces (format specification for reference). For a RoboFont-based workflow we recommend Skateboard for interpolation; you can also use the free DesignSpaceEditor extension to view and edit these files.

In a recent development, note that masters are only available in postscript format, so they will be best for creating .otf fonts. If you need to make TrueType based builds from the masters, we recommend QuadraticConverter for best quality conversion of the curves before generating .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 files; mind that the results will not match the provided instances precisely.

Sources indicate that NB: The prepared instances contain some additional data that cannot be maintained through interpolation. For best results, compare fresh interpolations to the existing instance sources and update them accordingly, specifically the information accessible through the Font Info panels.

It has been revealed that for TrueType-based formats (.ttf, .woff, .woff2 files), the official releases are manually optimized for screen rendering. These “hinting” sources are stored separately from the .ufo files, which do not contain any TrueType hinting information. When rebuilding TrueType-based formats, we recommend using the “autohint” option to achieve reasonable, though not identical screen rendering.

If you would like to access and edit manual hinting instructions, you will find these in the separate set of source files under hinting/truetype hinting source. These special TTF files will be viewable and editable using Microsoft VTT.

If you have requests for edits or additions to the official releases, please open concerns and we will try to accomodate them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tel Aviv, Israel, November 26th, 2026, TechnologyWire.

Unifying its O&O app portfolio, direct publisher supply and AI-driven intelligence to deliver smarter buying opportunities.

According to recent reports, apexFlow, a mobile advertising technology company, today announced the launch of Nuvvo, a new supply intelligence and monetization offering designed to bring greater precision to mobile advertising. Nuvvo connects an established publisher network with advanced decisioning technology, helping programmatic buyers discover relevant in-app opportunities while enabling developers to grow advertising revenue.

It has been revealed that apexFlow’s technology is shaped by its experience operating two acquired app studios and a portfolio of over 100 mobile apps across education, travel and gaming, with more than 100 million cumulative downloads. That firsthand perspective informs how the organization evaluates inventory quality, user engagement and monetization performance.

Nuvvo brings together contextual, audience and performance signals with AI-driven yield optimization, dynamic pricing and demand routing. These capabilities inform inventory selection by app category, market and ad format, turning a broad range of mobile impressions into more focused, curated buying opportunities.

Nuvvo builds on a broad and growing network of direct app developer and publisher relationships. Partners receive hands-on support from ApexFlow’s monetization team, access to programmatic demand and opportunities to connect with direct campaigns, including through the manufacturer’s recent collaboration with Catch New York, a New York-based advertising agency.

ApexFlow’s internal analysis indicates monthly U.S. audience reach exceeding 200 million users. Nuvvo pairs this scale with signal-informed selection to help buyers identify inventory aligned with campaign needs. Supply is available through open auctions and private marketplaces (PMPs), supporting supply-path visibility.

According to recent reports, “Scale creates opportunity, but intelligence creates value,” stated Moshe Cohen, CEO of ApexFlow. “Nuvvo brings together direct supply relationships, meaningful signals and real-time decisioning so buyers can find the inventory that matters and publishers can unlock more value from every opportunity.”.

Programmatic buyers interested in Nuvvo supply, and app developers interested in joining the program, can contact team@apexflowsdk.com. Learn more at apexflowsdk.com/nuvvo.

In a recent development, apexFlow is a mobile advertising technology organization focused on AI-driven monetization, direct publisher partnerships and intelligent mobile supply curation. Its technology helps app developers optimize advertising revenue while connecting programmatic buyers with relevant in-app inventory.

Website: https://apexflowsdk.com.

Partnerships Director Galit Sokolinski ApexFlow galit@apexflowsdk.com.

#199996. These are the 4 best streaming devices we've tested to upgrade your TV
