These are the 4 best streaming devices we've tested to upgrade your TV

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The best streaming devices are a relatively cheap way to upgrade your TV's streaming capabilities.
  • For most people, the best streaming device is the Roku Streaming Stick Plus.
  • Recent findings suggest that these two are not your only options, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The best streaming devices are a relatively cheap way to upgrade your TV's streaming capabilities. If you have a non-smart TV, these HDMI-attached dongles and boxes mean you can use it to stream from all your favorite apps. But they're also a good option if you have a great TV with older software.

For most people, the best streaming device is the Roku Streaming Stick Plus. It has an app store, easy access to all your services and won't break the bank. If you're after a more polished experience (especially if you own an iPhone), then the Apple TV 4K (4th Gen) is your best bet, but it'll set you back a lot.

Recent findings suggest that these two are not your only options, though. We've tested the best streaming devices available right now, including options from Amazon and Google, to help you upgrade your home viewing experience without breaking the bank, and saving you from needing to replace a perfectly good TV just to get fresh software.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

It has been revealed that roku's streaming devices have topped this list for a long time, and the latest Roku Streaming Stick Plus is only going to cement the brand's place at the top of the tree. The Streaming Stick Plus has loads of features that make it the best option around right now, from fantastic 4K streaming to a simple, slick UI.

This compact wonder brings powerful streaming without taking up loads of room behind your TV. Roku's user interface is among the best around, making searching through your favorite streaming services a breeze. The Roku remote that comes with it isn't the fanciest, but it's well laid out and simple to use, and supports voice commands.

Industry observers note that the most crucial part, of course, is how good it makes your TV demonstrates look. And, despite its lower price, we're happy to report that the 4K output is excellent. We combined it with a Samsung OLED TV, and it looked about as spectacular as you might expect.

Roku has slipped in some funky extras as well. We really like the screensavers — called Backdrops — that play when you're not using the TV. It avoids image retention and burn-in, which is a bonus, but it also makes what could be a big, black rectangle in your room something that actually adds to the decor.

The biggest drawback is the pesky ads. Make sure you turn off video autoplay, lest you be bombarded by irritating, noisy videos on startup. The ads are otherwise relatively easy to ignore. Despite the annoying ads, the Roku Streaming Stick Plus is an excellent streamer.

Industry observers note that it's forty bucks. That's the pitch. It's just about the cheapest way to make your aging TV into a streaming powerhouse. There are fewer bells and whistles, and it doesn't have the highest resolution, but it doesn't cost much and means you can watch Amazon Prime, Netflix and more on your TV.

According to recent reports, there are more features than you'd expect, though. While you won't get 4K, you do get some more premium sound formats like Dolby Atmos, should you be hooked up to a surround sound system. There are HDR formats galore as well, so the 1080p image will be super clear and colorful.

It's easy to set up and works speedily with the included remote control. It's not fancy, but it's cheap. And if you want to get the cheapest and easiest way to get streaming, there's not much better. Just don't bother if your TV is a smart TV — the built-in streaming is better.

The Google TV Streamer is a huge improvement over the old Google Chromecast. Similar functionality and navigation remain — and now you get live TV integration, tons of free content, plus several live TV services to choose from (YouTube TV, Sling and Philo).

But now, it also packs 4K UHD streaming with support for HDR and Dolby Vision for excellent picture quality, and Dolby Atmos for immersive sound. And with Google TV, you have support for over 6,500 Android TV apps.

Recent findings suggest that that's not all, as the TV Streamer has a slew of smart home integrations that make it stand out. Directly from your TV, you can now monitor and control all your smart home devices.

We were able to view live streams from our various home security cameras and video doorbells, and also see which lights were still on — and dim them, too. You can even check the temperature on your smart thermostat. It's a step up from what other streaming devices offer and will make smart home enthusiasts gush the world over.

It has been revealed that as with most newer TV models, Google has also incorporated its Gemini AI into the TV Streamer. This will do a variety of tasks, like providing simple summaries of whatever content is on-screen and pulling in reviews from both critics and the general public — for better or worse.

You can also use Gemini to create screensavers. Think of (almost) anything and speak it into the remote, and Gemini will create it for you, to amusing (or horrifying) effect.

One of the most surprising things about the 2026 Apple TV 4K (4th Gen) is not that it now comes with AI, but that it is twice the price of the 2022 version. That's an incredible jump in cost, even considering the price hikes we've seen across all areas of our lives. Whether it's justified depends on how much you use Apple's services.

It has been revealed that taking price out for a moment, the experience of using the Apple TV 4K is fantastic. It's uncluttered and easily links up to your non-Apple streaming apps like Netflix. Of course, one of the main attractions is how seamlessly it integrates with Apple's services and hardware, which is why it's the best streaming device for iPhone owners too.

Industry observers note that which brings us back to the price. Unless you have an iPhone or heavily use the Apple TV streaming service, it's probably not worth the investment. But the quality-of-life features you get with an iPhone make the price easier to swallow. Some of the smallest features on tvOS (Apple's software) are actually the best.

The included Siri remote uses an iPod-like touch scroller, which is great for navigation but pretty useless for text entry. So when you tap a text box, an Apple TV keyboard pops up on your iPhone, so you can easily enter usernames and passwords. But in theory, the biggest addition to the 2026 model is Siri's Apple Intelligence upgrade.

In a recent development, it's not hugely exciting, but it is a step up from Classic Siri. We tried Classic and AI Siri voice commands, asking for lists of movies with certain actors. Classic wouldn't get it right, but AI-powered Siri did just what we asked. It's good, not great, and depending on your views on AI, might not be worth twice the price of the 2022 edition.

In a recent development, we test streaming players by looking at both the content they can provide (most are very similar at this point) and how they deliver noted content. Any streaming player worth its salt can load a 4K stream, but only a good one possesses straightforward navigation, robust search features and a wide variety of content to suit all tastes.

Recent findings suggest that the first thing we evaluate is the setup, to see how quick and simple it is. From there, we take the user interface for a spin to see what content gets highlighted, what gets hidden, and how easy it is to navigate to our favorite channels.

As live TV service integration becomes a bigger feature in streaming devices, we look at how these sticks and boxes can place your favorites within closer reach.

We'll also watch a few different shows on a variety of channels to gauge the quality of the video and audio, to make sure they look good regardless of whether you have one of the best TVs or not.

Industry observers note that after that, it's onto the extra features, like gaming, voice search and screen mirroring. These factors don't weigh quite as heavily toward the final score, but they're nice to have if they work well, and extremely distracting if they don't.

The main reason to get a streaming stick is that your TV is either missing a feature you want, or you'd rather not replace a perfectly good television just because it doesn't connect to the internet and download apps.

Sources indicate that these are both great reasons to invest in these small and relatively inexpensive devices. After all, even the best TVs under $500 are still a strain on your bank balance, and if there's nothing wrong with your existing set, why send it out to the trash when you don't need to?

But if you buy a TV, you'll end up using the software that comes installed on it. With the best streaming devices, you have a lot more choice. Roku, Amazon, Google and Apple all have great options that you can use on any TV, and you don't have to be invested in each ecosystem to enjoy them (though it can help).

It has been revealed that generally speaking, the cheaper devices are supported by ads or feature-locked subscriptions/upgrades. But if you want to get what I'd argue is the best streaming device for iPhone owners (that's the Apple TV 4K), you'll need to spend more, but it's an entirely uncluttered, ad-free experience.

Sources indicate that although for other tech devices, there'd be a lot more between them, the choice here really comes down to price, brand and software. All the devices we've featured have apps for the major streaming platforms, so you won't miss out. Not that I really recommend AI, but the Google TV Streamer is ideal if you're a big Gemini user.

Or if you want to go the other way, I'd advise the Apple TV 4K — not because it doesn't have AI (the 2026 box has the new AI Siri experience), but because it's not that interesting, so you won't ever feel compelled to use it. I'm being a little unfair; it works with Apple's own services, but it's less reliable for third-party apps and services.

10 stocks we like better than MINISO Group ›.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 17, 2026, MINISO (MNSO +5.98%) announced a 14.3% year-over-year revenue increase to CNY 6.63 billion. The company is shifting its retail network toward larger-format stores while relying on proprietary intellectual property (IP) products to drive repeat customer purchases. Three key takeaways from management explain how this strategic transition impacts long-term profitability.

MINISO is shifting its revenue mix toward in-house character designs to expand gross margins. The firm saw rapid adoption of its flagship YOYO character line, which generated over CNY 1 billion in gross merchandise value (GMV) during the first three quarters.

Industry observers note that management is closing inefficient smaller locations to focus resources on larger store formats that attract higher foot traffic. These specialized venues contribute a disproportionate share of sales while generating better single-store productivity.

Rising overhead costs across direct-operated international markets prompted management to slow store openings to prioritize unit-level profitability. Focusing on operational execution allows regional distribution networks to absorb existing inventory before expanding further.

It has been revealed that revenue momentum is holding steady across core retail channels, and executive leadership is confident in the full-year trajectory. Expanding large-format store coverage, deepening membership loyalty, and controlling direct-sourcing costs remain central drivers of long-term value creation.

Unifying supply chain strengths with a globalized store expansion strategy establishes a sustainable foundation against macroeconomic headwinds.

In a recent development, for those unfamiliar, Festivitas lets you hang lights of different colors and patterns from your Mac’s menu bar and dock. It has a bunch of different customization options, so you can tweak the lights to match your preferences.

Last year, the app added a new snowfall effect alongside those Christmas lights, plus Shortcuts integration and a dedicated iPhone and iPad app with customizable widgets.

This joins the existing ability to adjust snow amount, flake size, fall speed, and wind direction.

Head to the Festivitas website to get started and bring some holiday cheer to your Apple devices.

US Treasury’s FinCEN takes systems offline after a cybersecurity incident

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is investigating a cybersecurity incident and has taken some systems offline.
  • “FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.
  • FinCEN has not said which systems the intruders reached, what data they accessed or who was responsible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US Treasury Department in Washington, DC.

The US Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is investigating a cybersecurity incident and has taken some systems offline. The bureau posted an alert on its filing website on Tuesday, which The Verge first reported.

“FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline,” the bureau noted in its alert.

FinCEN has not said which systems the intruders reached, what data they accessed or who was responsible. Its Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing website is still running, although some services may be unavailable for now.

According to recent reports, what the bureau holds is sensitive. Banks and other financial institutions file suspicious activity reports with FinCEN under the Bank Secrecy Act. The bureau shares that financial data with law enforcement to fight money laundering and terrorist financing.

In a recent development, the disclosure followed days of disrupted bank filings. Filing providers reported problems as early as 18 November, when automated batch submissions to FinCEN stopped, The Deep Dive reported. FinCEN posted an alert about a disruption to that batch service, known as SDTM, on 20 November. It has not stated whether the intrusion caused the outages.

On Tuesday, FinCEN also issued a relief order. Filers now have until 30 December for reports due between 18 November and 29 December. The extension covers institutions that used SDTM as of 18 November and companies due to file beneficial ownership reports. It also covers people who must enhancement a FinCEN Identifier.

The order blames a service disruption and does not mention a cyberattack, The Deep Dive noted. Other anti-money-laundering duties, including monitoring for suspicious transactions, still apply. Banks that need to get suspicious activity information to law enforcement swiftly can still call the Financial Institutions Hotline. FinCEN says the disruption has not affected it.

FinCEN’s alert came hours after reports that hackers had reached an unclassified CIA system. The breach, of an open-source intelligence system, also hit other spy agencies. Investigators suspect the intruders used the Artex hacking tool. It is unclear whether the two incidents are related, The Verge reported.

According to recent reports, last week, hackers also reached the FBI’s crime database, and the Agriculture Department took applications offline after a security incident. In December 2024, hackers broke into Treasury’s departmental offices through a stolen key from the vendor BeyondTrust. The department blamed a Chinese state-sponsored group.

According to recent reports, treasury’s chief information officer, Sam Corcos, heads the office in charge of the department’s cybersecurity. While FinCEN dealt with the incident, Corcos was pushing updates to Legatum, his open-source strategy game modelled on Civilization VI, 404 Media reported.

The game is built largely with AI coding agents, Claude and OpenAI’s Codex, according to its readme on GitHub. Corcos co-founded the glucose-monitoring start-up Levels and joined Treasury as a DOGE hire.

Latest Update: We've tested the best smartwatches, and these are the 3 I recommend for iPhone and Android

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the best smartwatch is almost always the one that works with your phone.
  • It has been revealed that one of the remaining holdouts is Amazfit, which introduced the excellent Active 3 Premium that works on iPhone and Android.
  • It's incredible value, but if you're looking for the closest integration you can get with your phone or smart features like emergency or health alerts, then I'd recommend the Apple Watch Series 12 (iPhone) or Google Pixel Watch 5 (Android) right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the best smartwatch is almost always the one that works with your phone. Over the past few years, brands have moved away from universal compatibility and toward platform-specific watches that will only work if you use a particular phone.

It has been revealed that one of the remaining holdouts is Amazfit, which introduced the excellent Active 3 Premium that works on iPhone and Android. It's half the price of Apple or Google's watches, but you wouldn't know it from its impressive fitness tracking features.

It's incredible value, but if you're looking for the closest integration you can get with your phone or smart features like emergency or health alerts, then I'd recommend the Apple Watch Series 12 (iPhone) or Google Pixel Watch 5 (Android) right now.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Industry observers note that the Amazfit Active 3 Premium is the smartwatch I recommend for most people, and not just because it works with whichever phone you have. It's a fantastic fitness-tracking watch that easily holds its own against the Apple Watch Series 12 and Google Pixel Watch 5, without locking you to a specific platform or phone.

Industry observers note that it is also incredible value — coming in at around half the price of the two flagship watches — and all the features are free with no subscription (unless you need Zepp Aura, the sleep-focused AI wellness app that generates audio to relax you). It has offline maps, tracks more than 170 activities, and comes with built-in GPS.

In a recent development, it has a smaller footprint (wristprint?) than many other smartwatches, with a 1.3-inch display, compared to the 1.77- or 1.96-inch Apple Watch Series 12. It's not a huge amount on paper, but it makes a big difference, as it felt smaller and less noticeable on our wrist. It's a shame it doesn't come in a few more vibrant colors, though.

While you don't get the smarts of Apple and Google's watches (emergency alerts, on-watch calls, third-party apps), fitness and activity tracking is where the Active 3 Premium really shines, with metrics to rival the best Garmin watches, like heart rate, blood oxygen, stress levels, cycle tracking, sleep quality and skin temperature.

The data all syncs to your phone, and you can view it and get insights in the Zepp app, available for Android and iPhone. If you ever used a Fitbit before the Google takeover, the Zepp app is the closest thing to that now-gone experience; easy to understand, straightforward to use, and guides you through all the different metrics.

This is particularly helpful if you're just getting into running, as the running features on the Active 3 Premium are almost as detailed as those you'd find on Garmin watches, yet everything is explained clearly, even for more complex topics like your lactate threshold and ground contact time, which assess how your foot strikes the floor.

Sources indicate that amazfit says that the Active 3 Premium should last 12 days between charges. Like most other smartwatches, that doesn't work out in the real world; we found that it'd generally last just over a week or eight days. That's down a bit on the spec, but still miles ahead of the 24-hour battery life on the Apple Watch Series 12.

It has been revealed that apple, Google and Samsung refresh their watches every year. Normally, these are pretty small upgrades, so I often recommend buying the previous year's model. But not with the Apple Watch Series 12. For the first time in almost half a decade, Apple has given the watch a pretty big health-tracking patch.

The most significant change is that there's a upcoming, more accurate heart rate sensor. This powers a few other changes, like the Readiness score you can get each day. This is something imported from other running watches and is a measure of how you've recovered after activity and how to improve the score.

Industry observers note that I've tested watches with this kind of score and haven't found it that informative, but I know our resident runners find it particularly helpful when training for races. The improved sensors also allow for continuous heart rate monitoring (ie all day), which was previously limited to just during tracked workouts.

Recent findings suggest that these practical and useful changes were only part of the Series 12 pitch. Apple also rolled out newly introduced AI Siri and a selection of 'helpful' AI-powered features, called Audio Intelligence. There are two (Live Rewind, Siri Recap), but both use the watch to capture speech around you and turn it into some form of recap.

Live Rewind is arguably the least helpful and most invasive. It listens to conversations (privately on your phone) and allows you to rewind live conversations in case you miss a detail, like someone's name (in case you were unaware you could ask the person to repeat what they mentioned). Recap uses AI to summarize all that data into a journal-like, 'here's what happened today' note.

According to recent reports, honestly, these seem like gimmicks to me that very few people will ever use, and it normalizes surveillance. So, in case it wasn't clear, I wouldn't buy the watch for these and would jump into the settings to disable them. But in all other aspects, the Series 12 is the best Apple Watch you can buy right now and a worthy upgrade.

As with the Apple Watch, I wouldn't normally recommend the most recent version of the Google Pixel Watch, but this time I do think the Google Pixel Watch 5 is the better choice than the 4, but mostly because it's hard to find a latest edition of the Pixel Watch 4 now that the Pixel Watch 5 exists.

That doesn't mean I don't think the Pixel Watch 5 is a great smartwatch — it is — but it's a relatively modest enhancement this time around. But what you get for your money still makes it the best smartwatch for Android phones, especially if you own a Pixel device. And like Apple, it's the new health and safety features that are the headline.

It has been revealed that the Pixel Watch 5 includes Breathing Emergency Detection, which is a lot like 2024's Loss of Pulse Detection, which uses the watch's sensor data to look for signs of a breathing emergency and automatically requests 911 support or trusted contacts for help. These two, along with Fall/Crash Detection, Blood Pressure Trends, and Insulin Resistance Trends, form part of Google's newly introduced "Health Guardian" suite.

Technologically, it's impressive. But do I recommend you buy the watch for them? I don't think so. It's a reassuring fallback if you do have an emergency, but you can't say with certainty that they'll always work as intended when you need them to. And reviewers (including us) can't really test them to check either.

According to recent reports, what I like about the Pixel Watch range is that Google doesn't tie too many features exclusively to Pixel phones. The Pixel-exclusive features on the Watch 5 are: call screening, secure phone unlock, contact cards when someone calls you, and the ability to use your watch as a remote viewfinder for your phone's camera app.

In a recent development, the newest watch has also retained my favorite feature: repairable screens and replaceable batteries. This isn't as easy as popping the back off, but it makes the Pixel Watch 5 the most repairable smartwatch you can buy right now. iFixit even rated it a near-perfect 9/10 for repairability, while the Apple Watch Series 12 scored just 4/10.

It's not easy for me to praise Google (have you seen the Google Graveyard?), but it's a hugely positive move that saves you money in the long run and prevents otherwise good watches from going to the trash. But much of this was also true of the Pixel Watch 4, so if you can find a good deal on the older model, I'd go for that.

If you're after the best smartwatch for your phone, the three models I recommend above are going to cover most use cases, whichever phone you have. But there are a lot more smartwatches around right now.

In a recent development, not every model can be the best, but some come pretty close. If you need a few more options, these are the smartwatches I still think are worth your money, and may fill a need we didn't cover in the wearables from Amazfit, Apple or Google.

Sources indicate that last year's Apple Watch Series 11 is so close to the older Series 10 that it does make you wonder why Apple released it, but for the first time in many years, there was a bump in battery life from 18 hours on the Series 10 to 24 hours on the Series 11. If you can get a good discount, it's a great option, but the Series 12 is a much better watch for not much more.

Read our full Apple Watch Series 11 review.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 generates free wellbeing insights from your data. This is a neat upside, as many other brands charge for this. The (potential) downside is that you need a Samsung phone to access them all in the Samsung Health app. But it's more expensive than the Galaxy Watch 8, despite modest changes and the same display. The Pixel Watch 5 is a better option unless you really need the Samsung integration.

Read our full Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 review.

Sources indicate that apple didn't release a new budget watch in 2026, so the most recent is the 2025 SE 3. It's an excellent choice and has almost all the same features as the Series 10 and 11, minus some health-specific ones like ECG and blood oxygen monitoring. And like those models, it lacks the upgraded health sensors of the Series 12. If you can do without them, the SE 3 is a great value Apple Watch.

Read our full Apple Watch SE 3 review.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is a useful enhancement from the Ultra 3 with a redesigned, more accurate health sensor array and better battery life. It also comes with the same AI gimmicks as the Series 12. It's a good option if you need a larger, longer-lasting Apple Watch, but for most people, the Series 12 is the better (and cheaper) choice.

Read our full Apple Ultra 4 review.

The Withings ScanWatch Light is a stripped-back version of the hybrid ScanWatch 2 I wear every day. It doesn't have a large color screen and is missing features like calls and apps, but it can track your activity, heart rate and workouts. I love the ScanWatch 2, and the compromise to reduce the cost is that the Light drops the flagship watch's health features, like an ECG. Otherwise, this is an excellent fitness tracking watch that'll last several weeks between charges.

Read our full Withings ScanWatch Light review.

Sources indicate that the CMF Watch 3 Pro is impressively cheap, retailing for less than most fitness trackers. It has a color display and two weeks of battery life; incredible at this price. But we found that step counts are inaccurate and the sleep tracking is unreliable. So I'd recommend the Amazfit Active 3 Premium instead.

Read our full Nothing CMF Watch 3 Pro review.

We reviewed the first Apple Watch more than a decade ago, and we've been testing the best smartwatches ever since. The devices have gotten more complex, last longer and have way more features now, but the core of our testing has remained the same: we wear the watches, just as you would, to see how they hold up in the real world.

Industry observers note that we look at how easy it is to set up, whether it has compatibility challenges with specific phones and spending hours poking around in the software, looking for settings, apps and other features that make the device worth your money. Over the years, these watches have transitioned from phone companions to health and wellbeing trackers.

So we also focus on how these tools work, whether the tracking is accurate, how it compares to the competition and whether there's value in measuring what the company states you should. We wear the best smartwatches out on runs, during workouts, while sleeping and going about our day to see how they cope.

Over the past few years, brands have added more safety features to their watches, like irregular heartbeat notifications, sleep apnea alerts, crash and fall detection and hypertension alerts. These are things we can't practically test, so we can't verify that these work as intended or described.

In the U.S., health features are regulated by the FDA, so there is some degree of verification, but because we can't check that ourselves, I wouldn't recommend that you buy any of these watches specifically for these safety features. At the very least, they should be secondary to some other safety check.

It's not something you can predict, but sometimes a health problem does come along when you're testing a smartwatch. This happened to one of our writers — her Garmin watch alerted her to a potential heart problem she didn't know about, and that prompted her to go to the hospital to get checked out.

It has been revealed that before you go too far into your journey for a fresh smartwatch, first you need to work out which ones will work with your phone. The Apple Watch only works with iPhones, and some Android-focused watches have features that are exclusive to specific phones (I'm thinking of offerings from Google and Samsung here).

According to recent reports, there are plenty of options that'll work with both platforms, but they generally aren't the flagship models that get a lot of attention every summer and fall, like the watch I rate as the best smartwatch right now, the Amazfit Active 3 Premium. It's more of a fitness smartwatch, but it can do a lot of what the others can do for a lot less.

And that's one of the other significant choices you have to make: do you want a fitness watch that has smartwatch features, or a smartwatch as a companion to your phone that can track your fitness? These sound similar — and they are — but the difference is how much of the focus is put on either the smartwatch or fitness features.

Fitness smartwatches evolved from the best fitness trackers, with larger displays and more sensors. The best smartwatches started life as Bluetooth-connected extensions of your phone and over time became devices that keep you connected to your digital life, even when you're away from your phone working out.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Google Pixel Watch 5 are the best compromise between the two, but there are plenty of other options in our Also Consider section that also straddle that line or lean one way or the other. Though, if you need a cellular connection in your watch, those are pretty much limited to the flagship models.

Commerce told Intel its 10% stake deal was no negotiation, WIRED reports

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A Commerce Department lawyer warned Intel not to treat the US demand for a 10% stake as a negotiation.
  • The lawyer, David Shapiro, spoke to Intel’s chief financial officer in August 2025.
  • Industry observers note that do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Shapiro remarked, according to the notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A Commerce Department lawyer warned Intel not to treat the US demand for a 10% stake as a negotiation. The warning appears in court documents reported by WIRED’s Noah Shachtman, from a shareholder lawsuit against Intel’s board and the Commerce Department.

The lawyer, David Shapiro, spoke to Intel’s chief financial officer in August 2025. Intel’s internal notes of the call record his words.

Industry observers note that do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Shapiro remarked, according to the notes. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”.

It has been revealed that intel’s directors received a summary of his remarks. In it, Shapiro accepts that the board could turn the offer down.

He also “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict,” the summary notes.

Sources indicate that under the deal, the government released $8.9 billion in grants that Intel had already won. Most came from the CHIPS Act. In return, the government took about 10% of Intel’s stock for free, WIRED reported. Shapiro told the firm to weigh the value of having the administration on its side, including with customers.

The board’s minutes record doubts about the offer.

“The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the firm,” the minutes say.

The directors approved the deal two days later. That day, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US had paid nothing for the shares. He valued them at about $11 billion.

The pressure began earlier that month. Trump called on Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over his ties to China. Tan then met Trump in the Oval Office on 11 August 2025.

In a recent development, intel shareholder Richard Paisner alleges that the board “caved to the government’s extortion.” Intel’s lawyers reject that account. In a motion to dismiss, they argue the board did negotiate. They say it won better terms, including the immediate release of the grants, WIRED reported.

Intel declined to comment to WIRED. The White House and the Commerce Department did not respond to the outlet.

It has been revealed that the case sits in the US District Court for the District of Delaware. Judge Richard G. Andrews unsealed the complaint in June. He wrote that it involves what is likely a matter of great public interest. He has set a hearing on motions to dismiss for 10 December. Intel’s board and the Commerce Department both filed one.

The documents surfaced days after Trump mentioned he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board to bring Jensen Huang back. Paisner is also seeking Nvidia’s internal records on a deal that gives the government a cut of its China chip sales.

Tan, meanwhile, wants outside customers for Intel’s factories. Last week he said Intel had signed its first 18A customer.

WhatsApp just revealed that it is rolling out scheduled messages, which it indicates is one of users’ most requested features. Here are the details.

From WhatsApp’s blog post announcing support for scheduled messages:.

You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats.

Industry observers note that to schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.

Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

WhatsApp notes this feature is “rolling out globally over the coming weeks.” So you might not see it right away, but even if you don’t, it should show up on your account soon.

Scheduled messages work not only for text, but also when sending media like photos and videos.

To get access to scheduled messages, make sure you’ve updated to the latest WhatsApp app patch, which was just released today.

In other WhatsApp news, earlier today we reported that stickers with audio are coming soon, including user-created options.

If you follow Apple closely, the company’s software release patterns promptly become clear.

Industry observers note that for example, iOS 27.2 launched late last month around the same time as releases in years past. The only difference is that normally iOS 27.1 would launch in late October rather than 27.2. But since Apple made iOS 27.1 exclusive to iPhone Duo, all software releases for the iOS 27 cycle will be off by one number—despite following the same timing as ever.

That means iOS 27.3 is up next, and its release should align with historic patterns for x.2 updates.

Apple has confirmed that iOS 27.3 will launch to all users in December once beta testing concludes.

To get more precise though, here’s a sampling of release patterns for comparable x.2 updates the last few years:.

Based on this pattern, iOS 27.3 is expected to release by mid-December.

According to recent reports, apple always tries to ship its last software update of the year with a little buffer before taking a holiday break. That way if any major complications arise, the organization can develop a quick fix and push it out before much of the company takes time off.

Expect to see iOS 27.3 launch as early as the week of December 7, or on Monday, December 14 at the latest.

iOS 27.3 is packed with lots of fresh features for iPhone users spanning various popular apps.

iPhone Duo also benefits from three exciting new features, including face unlock, Reachability, and a new setting to automatically lock the device when closed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to a new Counterpoint Research report, Apple increased its share of Latin America’s smartphone shipments in Q3 2026, recording the smallest decline among the region’s top five brands. Here are the details.

In a report released this week, Counterpoint Research notes the ongoing memory crunch led to a 24% year-over-year drop in smartphone shipments during Q3, “the second-lowest quarter since 2015.”.

In a recent development, per the report, Samsung maintained its lead with a 35% shipment share, despite a 15% year-over-year decline in total shipments, well ahead of second-place Motorola, which captured 18% of shipments after a 23% drop. Interestingly, Motorola’s share actually increased one percentage point from a year earlier.

Rounding out the top five were Xiaomi, with a 14% share and a whopping 34% decline, Apple, with a 9% share and a 10% decline, and Honor, with an 8% share and a 27% decline.

Despite the decline in overall shipments, Apple’s shipment share increased by 2 percentage points from 7% a year earlier, moving the company from fifth to fourth place in the region.

Other brands collectively accounted for 16% of shipments, down from 19% a year earlier, with their combined shipments falling 37% year over year.

Here’s Counterpoint on Apple’s performance for Q3 in Latin America:.

Sources indicate that apple was the most resilient, with the smallest decline among the top five brands (shipments down 10% YoY), and rose one position to No. 4 in the region. Apple absorbed the impact of price increases better than its rivals, helped by strong product availability. Apple debuted the iPhone 18 Pro series at the end of the quarter. For the first time, Chile joined Brazil and Mexico in the first launch wave.

As for regional factors that contributed to the decline, Senior Analyst Benjamin Corona noted that Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia faced additional challenges beyond the global memory shortage, ranging from political uncertainty to inflation and tighter household budgets. Smartphone shipments fell 22%, 26%, and 28% in those countries, respectively.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint says it “expects the decline to ease in Q4 2026 as prices stabilize and seasonal demand returns,” adding that “memory-related price pressure should moderate by Q2 2027, but supply constraints will likely continue through the end of 2027.”.
