💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a upcoming speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms.
  • Wispr Flow this week released Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the company says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.
  • In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a upcoming speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details.

Wispr Flow this week released Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the company says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.

In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.

According to the firm, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken.

Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions:.

Canto-2 recovers hard names and terms accurately nearly 7 of 10 times, without more false insertions. It makes a third fewer mistakes across 14 languages, and has the lowest Hindi error rate of any multilingual model on Hugging Face’s open benchmark. It is 10 times the scale of Canto-1, and our biggest step yet toward dictation that’s ready to send without a single edit.

According to the company, the percentage of difficult names and terms correctly recognized went from 41% to 69% between Canto-1 and Canto-2, “without inserting them more often.” It added that this improvement holds up even as the user’s custom dictionary grows, with the upcoming model correctly recognizing 92% of easier terms even with 1,000 saved entries.

Wispr also noted that it trained Canto-2 to handle real-world dictation conditions, including background noise, laptop and phone microphones, and sentences that restart halfway through, rather than relying solely on clean recordings of scripted speech.

When tested using Hugging Face’s public multilingual benchmark, Canto-2 achieved results that would have placed it third overall as of November 9. However, Wispr conducted the evaluation itself, and the model has not yet been officially added to the leaderboard as of today, November 25.

In its own internal benchmarks, the company notes Canto-2 achieved the lowest average error rate among the competing models it tested across 14 languages.

Canto-2 is now available to Wispr Flow people on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in the Americas, with the rollout to other regions underway.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
  • After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
  • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a fresh Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber states that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Industry observers note that record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

Uber claims the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Industry observers note that not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Uber notes it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

  • MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following reports that its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors, Apple has removed the popular Chinese AI companion app Talkie from the App Store. Here are the details.

As reported by the South China Morning Post, Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”.

MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.

In 2023, the Shanghai-based organization released Talkie through Subsup, a Singaporean subsidiary. According to Chinese research firm Unique Research, Talkie had “almost 11 million monthly active users across its website and app as of October,” the South China Morning Post notes.

Now, however, the app is facing scrutiny following a joint investigation by the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Australian broadcaster ABC News, which found that Talkie’s AI-generated characters allegedly engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors, including “degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play.”.

According to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, in addition to inappropriate romantic interactions, the investigation uncovered conversations involving verbal abuse, violence, and controlling behavior.

In one case, a chatbot told a 12-year-old girl: “You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”.

The investigation also documented the experiences of two sisters, aged 10 and 13, whose mother discovered more than 40 conversations with Talkie characters involving violence, aggressive behavior, and attempts to control girls.

To make matters worse, the investigation also raised concerns about how Talkie handles owners’ personal data, including their conversations with AI characters.

Following the investigation, Apple confirmed that it had removed Talkie from App Stores worldwide for including sexual content, “though it did not say whether this related to sexual content served to minors,” the South China Morning Post noted.

Ironically, the report also notes that Talkie saw a sharp decline in downloads amid complaints about stricter age verification measures introduced in recent months. According to Unique Research, fresh downloads fell by 32.2% in October compared to the previous month.

Today’s news comes amid increasing scrutiny of AI chatbots, particularly their potential risks in interactions with minors.

Earlier this year, Elon Musk’s Grok faced widespread criticism after users exploited its image-generation capabilities to create sexualized images of real people, including minors.

Apple never pulled X or Grok from the App Store, though it did threaten to remove the latter unless xAI addressed violations of its App Store guidelines.

Meanwhile, Character.AI has faced multiple lawsuits over its chatbots’ interactions with minors, including one filed by a mother who alleged that one of its chatbots contributed to her 14-year-old son’s suicide.

Coincidentally, Character AI also made headlines today after a coalition of 42 US attorneys general challenged the company’s plans to auction off its platform and the private conversations of more than 21 million US accounts (including 2.1 million registered to minors) as part of its bankruptcy proceedings.

Yesterday, Fresh York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of toys with built-in AI chatbots, including dolls, stuffed animals, and robots capable of holding conversations with children.

The law, which takes effect in February 2027, is aimed at protecting children from potentially harmful interactions with AI.

In a recent development, need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected].

FinVolution (FINV -2.02%) reported a sequential contraction in loan volume as management prioritized asset quality and funding stability amid regulatory and institutional shifts in the Chinese market. The company stated that its diversification strategy successfully used growing international operations to offset domestic headwinds, with overseas revenue increasing to 37% of the total mix. In China, management responded to a tightening institutional funding market and reduced collection capacity by restricting credit to high-quality existing borrowers and upgrading risk models. Operational progress continued in international markets, including Indonesia and Australia, where the company expanded its offline presence and utilized open banking data to refine credit pricing. FinVolution maintained a liquidity position of RMB 8.4 billion while continuing to return capital through share repurchases and the retirement of convertible debt.

Operator: Thank you for participating in the Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call for FinVolution Group. [Operator Instructions] Today's conference call is being recorded. I'll now turn the call over to your host, Yam Cheng, Head of Capital Markets of the manufacturer. Yam, please go ahead.

These non-GAAP financial measures are not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. For information about these non-GAAP measures and reconciliation to GAAP measures, please refer to our earnings press release. Further information regarding these and other risks and uncertainties are included in the company's filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer does not assume any obligation to patch any forward-looking statements, except as required under applicable law. Finally, we have also posted our results presentation on our website. I'll now turn over to our CEO, Tim. Please go ahead, Tim.

Tiezheng Li: Thanks, Yam. Welcome to our third quarter 2024 (sic) [ 2026 ] earnings call. Some strategies are built for comfort. Ours was built for quarters selective. For nearly a decade, we have spread our business across markets, economies, and regulatory regimes not because anyone of them was under pressure, but because we knew that one day, one of them could be. This quarter, that day came in China and while our domestic business absorbed the shock, our overseas business kept growing and kept they growing. Once again, diversification carried us. The third quarter was a challenging transition period for China business.

Recent findings suggest that in July, a credit event at another platform eroded confidence across China's loan facilitation industry and financial institutions sharply put back funding to the sector. From late July, a nationwide campaign against collection agencies cut collection capacity and efficiency. Together, these 2 developments hit our China business on 3 fronts: advance funding supply, credit performance, and loan origination. We responded as we remarked we would on last quarter's call, prioritizing funding stability and asset quality over growth. We tightened underwriting and directed to funding available to us towards our best quality existing borrowers. As a result, group's loan volume contracted to approximately RMB 20 billion, down 56% sequentially, driven mainly by the slowdown in China.

Meanwhile, our diversification strategy continued to work as intended. Overseas volume grew 11% year-over-year to RMB 4 billion. Revenue rose to RMB 949 million, 11% year-over-year and 2% sequentially. Overseas now account for 37% of group revenue. More importantly, this growth is also profitable. Overseas operating profit more than doubled year-over-year to RMB 62 million. Now let me take each segment in turn, starting with Chinese Mainland. Regulation now reaches into every part of the lending process. The newly introduced financing cost disclosure rules took effect on August 1 and the new online marketing rules on September 30.

Compliance is our first priority, and we have worked with our bank partners on loan products and the referral flows that meet the new requirements. China loan volume contracted to approximately RMB 16 billion, down 61% sequentially, reflecting tighter funding supply and the elevated credit risk across the industry. On funding, institution turned risk averse from July and the supply fell sharply. Our priority throughout the quarter was to restore funding and keep it aligned with loan origination. We gave our bank partners full visibility into our fund flows and processes, and adopted our partnership model to their requirements and risk appetite, including closed-loop payment controls and additional checks.

As a result, funding supply recovered steadily from its July low through August and September. Though it remains below normal level in early October, we and other lending platform also completed compliance self-checks on fund flows and submitted clean audit reports from independent third-party firms to the National Internet Finance Association of China. We believe this marks an crucial step in restoring institutional confidence across the industry and our compliance record positioned us well as funding partners become more selective. On risk, our metrics improved steadily throughout the first half of 2026.

The trend reversed in July, driven by 2 industry-wide factors: First, as funding tightened across the industry, borrowers had less access to credit and the repayment to legacy loans generally weakened; Second, the collection campaign we flagged last quarter reduced recovery capacity and pushed the delinquencies higher. In response, we upgraded our risk models and tightened underwriting further during the quarter. Our approach was simple, lend less, lend it to the people we know, and keep bad actors out. I would like to further elaborate on this in a bit. In this elevated risk environment, we expect legacy loans to continue to weigh on credit costs.

According to recent reports, looking ahead, we will maintain our compliance-first risk-focused approach through this reset in China with asset quality as the core priority. Now let's move on to the overseas segment. Our overseas business maintained its growth momentum with volume up 5% sequentially to RMB 4 billion. Our diversification markets portfolio continued to act as a buffer against country-specific headwinds. In Indonesia, Indonesia remains our largest overseas market. Offline Buy Now, Pay Later accounted for approximately 31% of volume this quarter, up from approximately 25% in prior quarter and 10% a year ago. The shift is deliberate.

In a recent development, offline Buy Now, Pay Later is originated at point of sales, so the use of funds is easier to verify and the customer relationship runs through a merchant network rather than a paid traffic. With acquisition costs and regulatory scrutiny both rising, that is a more durable way to grow. In the Philippines, volume edged down 5% sequentially as the business cycled under the newly introduced rate cap. Credit performance came in better than expected, helped by another typhoon season and the conservative underwriting we put in place over the past 3 quarters. We believe the transition to the lower rate cap is largely complete, and we look to restart growth in the coming quarters. In Australia, volume grew 21% sequentially.

It has been revealed that the growth came with a better customer mix with higher quality middle to large loans rising to around half of the portfolio. The key was the deeper integration with Australia's open banking regime, which gave us verified transaction level data on income, spending, and existing debt in place of self-declared inputs. That data works in 2 directions. We can approach good credit applicants we would previously have declined, and we can price and size credit limits more accurately for everyone else. As a result, conversion among good credit applicants improved while our underwriting standards held firm. On the foundation, we are now adding larger ticket products for borrowers with stronger credit profiles, and we expect the mix shift to continue.

Technology remains to -- how we run this business and this quarter, it mattered more than ever. As the collection campaign cut industry capacity, our AI collection agents helped offset part of the lost external capacity. Two of our AI applicants, including our customer service agent built on our own large language model, [ RAG Fin ] were also named exemplary cases in Shanghai's 2026 Collection Of Outstanding Artificial Intelligence Applicants. The agents has served more than 100 million owners with a roughly 7% relative increase in self-service resolution. To close, at the start of this year, we said we would move through 2026 with patience and caution.

China's reset is still underway, and we expect the industry to keep evolving around risk, funding, and regulation. We expect to come through it with a clearly more resilient China business and overseas business that contributes a growing share of our profit. We entered this period with RMB 8.4 billion in cash and short-term investments and a strong diversified overseas business that continues to grow. I will now turn the call over to our CFO, Alexis, for a deeper look at the numbers.

Jiayuan Xu: Thank you, Tim, and hello, everyone. Let me go through our key results for the third quarter. Please refer to our earnings press release for further details. I will cover each segment and then the group results. First, China. Our priorities this quarter were funding stability, risk mitigation, and cost discipline. China revenue was RMB 1.5 billion, down 38% sequentially, reflecting a smaller loan book, partially cushioned by deferred revenue from legacy loan cohorts. Take rate for this quarter landed at around 2.9%, down 30 basis points from the second quarter due to rising credit and funding costs.

Our credit risk indicators remain elevated for 2 reasons: The industry-wide funding squeeze and the collection campaign that began at the end of July. For loans originated in the third quarter, we expect vintage cost of 3.5% compared with 2.7% for the second quarter. Early risk indicators showed a smaller -- a similar trend. Network delinquency rose from 5.3% to 6.4%, mainly from legacy loans originated before funding tightened. The 30-day collection rate fell from 89% to 85% as collection capacity across the industry strength. As a result, CM2 rose from 0.56% to 0.92%.

According to recent reports, as Tim mentioned, we are tightening risk controls on 3 fronts: be selective with new customers, lend to the people we know best, and shut out fraud. First, our new customers with funding tight across the industry, risk surface faster and the quality of the new customer traffic deteriorated. So we became much more selective. We tracked how stress were spread across the industry and used those signals to adjust our approval strategy and the credit limit models early. We shifted our channel mix toward higher quality source and cut off high-risk traffic. Second, our existing customers in a tougher environment, we focus on funding borrowers we know well.

But even familiar borrowers can change quickly when credit drives up elsewhere. So we looked more closely at 3 warning signs: Borrowing from multiple plans, pipe platforms, high debt relative to income, and unstable repayment. We re-evaluated the portfolio by risk-adjusted return, reduced exposure to borrowers showing these signs, and moved the credit limits to those with proven track records. We also added specific controls for borrowers who repeatedly paid a few days later and early signs of stress. This keeps our risk exposure contained. Put credit in steady hands and ease pressure on collections. Third on fraud. When credit tightens, fraud becomes more organized. First through intermediaries and the connected networks that one-by-one application checks cannot catch.

According to recent reports, we strengthened pattern detection across money flows, intermediary behavior, application networks, and the devices. We will remain vigilant as we entered the fourth quarter and continue to prioritize loan quality. During the quarter, funding costs also rose from 3.7% to about 4.3% as the tight supply pushed up the cost of funding from a low base. We work closely with our funding partners to restore supply, while funding has not yet returned to normal level. It has recovered to a level sufficient for our current risk appetite and origination strategy. Moving on to overseas. Operating profit was RMB 62 million, up 15% sequentially and more than double the prior year level.

Demand remained resilient, and we added 2.8 million new borrowers, up 28% sequentially. That mentioned, the macro backdrop across our markets has become more challenging. Higher oil prices are driving inflation and monetary policy is tightening across the region. We are managing each market with that environment. In Indonesia, the rupiah has become under sustained pressure and the Bank Indonesia has raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to year high 6% to support the currency. Consumer confidence has softened with the index falling from 127 in July -- in January to 120 in October. We are monitoring credit quality closely and are ready to adjust our risk strategy early if conditions warrant.

Industry observers note that in the Philippines, inflation rose to 7.2% in September and the Central Bank has raised 4x in a row, most recently to 5.5%. As they scaled back origination ahead of this, we are well-positioned to restart growth at a measured pace. In Australia, the Reserve Bank has raised its cash rate 5x this year to 4.85%, and though we are mindful of the pressure, this puts out household budgets. Even so, demand for digital credit adoption remains strong, and we expect Australia to keep contributing to both growth and profit. Overseas operating profit for the first 9 months totaled about RMB 161 million, and we remain on track for our full year target of about USD 30 million in EBITDA.

And at the group level, net revenue was RMB 2.6 billion, down 25% sequentially. Operating expenses were RMB 1,048 million, down 27% sequentially, mainly due to lower sales and marketing spend as we serve more repeat customers through our own app rather than paid traffic. Total provision expense was broadly flat at RMB 1.35 billion despite lower origination, reflecting higher credit costs on legacy loans. Net profit was RMB 206 million, down 52%. Our balance sheet remains liquid and strong. Cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 8.4 billion. Our leverage ratio, defined as risk-bearing loan balance divided by shareholders' equity was 1.5x, a historical low. Our shareholder returns -- our capital allocation policy is unchanged.

Our current priority is to meet the operational needs of our business while optimizing our cost of debt. We repurchased USD 4.3 million of shares in the third quarter, bringing repurchase for the first 9 months to USD 71.1 million. In October, we prioritized capital toward our convertible senior notes, repurchasing about USD 19 million, which reduces our debt and the potential dilution. We remain committed to returning capital to shareholders based on sustainable normalized earnings and cash flow. Now to our outlook. Despite the third quarter's disruptions, group revenue reached RMB 9.2 billion for the first 3 quarters.

Industry observers note that we are, therefore, reiterating our full year revenue guidance of RMB 11.5 billion to RMB 12.9 billion and expect to land at the lower end of that range. This reflects our current and preliminary views subject to any changes to the operating environment. To sum up, the third quarter demonstrated both the cost of China's reset and the value of the choices we made before and during it. We cut volume early, tightened risk, and amended our funding relationships. We believe that the new environment will favor players with strong compliance discipline and operational know-how. Meanwhile, our overseas business continued to grow both its top and bottom lines.

Recent findings suggest that we are clear-eyed about the domestic challenges ahead and firmly committed to disciplined execution through the coming quarters with our focus on long-term returns for our shareholders. That concludes my prepared remarks. We will now open the call to the questions. Operator, please continue.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Dennis Bay of UBS.

Weizhou Bai: [Foreign Language] This is Dennis from UBS. I have 2 questions. The first is on the domestic funding environment. Could you please give us an enhancement on the recovery in domestic funding availability? And looking ahead into Q4, how do you expect funding costs and transaction volume to trend? Second is on your overseas business. We noticed that the overseas revenue continued to increase as a percentage of the group's total revenue in Q3. How do you see the long-term trend or long-term growth perspectives for your overseas business? And more specifically, what are the key opportunities and challenges in Indonesia and the Philippines?

It has been revealed that jiayuan Xu: I will take your first question, and Tim will take your second question. And your first question is about the funding. Let me take this in order. Where funding stands now then look on cross and volume. Funding has gradually recovered from its low in late July, but as credit risk picked up across the industry, we further tightened our underwriting standards. So the fundings, we can now say broadly match the volume we are comfortable originating. And let me give you a bit of context on the recovery. Back in late July, many of our funding partners were reviewing how many move through their partners' platforms.

Industry observers note that so we work them through each step from loan disbursement to payment and the repayment. Some institutions completed their reviews and patch their systems, funding started to come back in August gradually. So you can see how that played out in our monthly volumes. New loan volume every month for the first half of July was still strong, but the second half was weak. And since the low in July volume recovered in August and September onwards, so starting from July, monthly volume dropped by about 10% to August and then grew by 15% in September. For the third quarter as a whole, transaction volume in China was down about 60% quarter-over-quarter.

Recent findings suggest that it reflects the early pullback in funding and the rising credit risk. And then turning to the fourth quarter. Funding supply was basically stable through October and into November. In October, we also submitted a report, as we mentioned, about our funding flows to the National Internet Finance Association of China. And that really help us to comfort our funding partners. And in terms of the funding cost, tighter supply across the industry pushed our funding cost up from about 3.7% in second quarter to about 4.3% in the third quarter, an increase of 60 bps it will take time for financial institutions to regain their risk appetite.

It has been revealed that so we expect our funding cost to stay elevated in the fourth quarter, maybe slightly above the Q3 level. And for the fourth quarter volume, given the regulatory environment and still elevated industry risk, our priority, as we have mentioned, is the quality, not short-term scale. So the pace of any recovery will depend on the quality of the loans we can originate and the expected returns. We will prioritize higher-quality existing borrowers with a consistent repayment record, and we will keep underwriting tight for newly introduced borrowers. That's the approach how we protect the quality of the book where the market settles and as it positions us well for durable growth as conditions improve. Okay.

So that's for the first question.

Tiezheng Li: Yes. Dennis, I will answer the question. The second question is about our global expansion and the opportunity and the challenge about the developing market. Let me make 3 points. First, where we are. We started in Indonesia in 2018 and took what we learned to the business in 2019. And then we entered Australia through the Fundo application after the COVID. Right now, looking back, overseas revenue was about 20% in 2024 and about 25% in 2025. This time, for the first 9 months of this year, it reached 31%. So we already met the 30% target we set for the year. And our long-term goal is more than 50%.

Sources indicate that and more importantly, this growth is now turning into profit. All 3 markets are profitable at the operating level. Together, they made USD 24 million in the first 9 months. So we are on track of our full year target of around $30 million. International is no longer just a revenue. It's a revenue and profit story. And second, what's the opportunity and how the strategy is evolving. I think 2 things are changing and where we operate and who we are, who we serve. On the market, we've gone from developed market into a developed one. The different growth risk profitability, and that's what makes them complementary.

Sources indicate that and on the customer side, we start with small online cash loans, and we are now moving towards better quality borrowers with larger loans and longer terms. And in Indonesia, our multi-finance license let us do offline Buy Now, Pay Later which was 31% of our Indonesia volume in Q3. In the Philippines, we are beyond -- going beyond cash loans with products like Buy Now, Pay Later card. The aim in both is higher customer lifetime value and better profitability. And the third, the challenges, I'd like to highlight 2. One is from regulation. In the developing markets, it can be changed swiftly. A rate cap change, for example, can slow growth in short term.

According to recent reports, but we've been through this more than once last year, when Indonesia was affected. The Philippines helped offset it. This year, the Philippines is adjusting and the Indonesia and Australia are picking up the growth. That's why the portfolio matters. The other is the macro side, both Indonesia and the Philippines, face inflation and currency pressure and the geopolitical environment adds to that. So we watch local conditions closely and adjust our pace in each market. On currency, we match local currency assets with local currency liability. So that limits the impact on our group. So overall, we are confident in Indonesia and the Philippines.

Credit penetration is still low, and we were in the early both markets with years of local experience in risk and customer acquisition. So that gave us a solid base for steady sustainable growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Claire Ouyang from Goldman Sachs.

Claire Ouyang: [Foreign Language] This is Claire Ouyang from Goldman Sachs. My question is about the asset quality for domestic business. What are the main drivers behind the recent pickup in credit risk? As you head into Q4, how are these latest risk indicators trending? Are you seeing any signs of stabilization?

Jiayuan Xu: Thanks, Claire. I will take your questions. Yes, changes across the industry are starting to affect our existing loan book. That's the main reason credit risk has picked up. When funding tightened across the industry in July, some borrowers with high debt levels started to face liquidity pressure. So over time, it made it harder for them to keep up with payments on loans they had already taken out. And at the same time, changes in the collection environment made it harder to recover overdue payments. Together, these 2 factors put considerable pressure on asset quality across the industry in Q3. Let me put some numbers around it.

Recent findings suggest that our day 1 delinquency rate rose 21% quarter-over-quarter from 5.26% in second quarter to 6.35% in the third quarter. Our 30-day collection rate fell from 89.4% to 85.5% and our CM2 flow rate rose from 0.56% to 0.92%. Our vintage estimate for loans originated in Q3 is 3.5%, up 80 basis points from the Q2 vintage. In terms of how we have responded, we started to tighten our risk controls in July and reduced our exposure further in August and September, shifting our focus from volume growth to asset quality. As we have mentioned, we have tightened underwriting for newly introduced borrowers, refined how we manage existing borrowers, and strengthened our fraud controls.

We are also taking a close look at expected credit cost and profitability across the borrower segments and the loan portfolios. That really helped us adjust the pace of origination and give priority to loans with better risk-adjusted returns while keeping our overall exposure in check. But it takes time for those changes to show up across the portfolio. Our loans have an average tenure of 8 to 9 months. So it typically takes about 2 to 3 quarters for risk in the existing book to work its way out. We have already tightened underwriting on new loans, but it will take time to see the full effect on the whole asset quality. So turning to the fourth quarter.

Our latest data reveals the CM2 flow rate, one of our early risk indicators reached a recent high at the end of September. And in October, it fell 6% from September. That was mainly due to a modest improvement in our 30-day collection rate. The collection rate is a very key part. So I'd like to add some more details. We have adjusted both our staffing and our strategy in response to our early pressure on recoveries. First, we have added staff to our in-house collections team and focus more resources on loans that are 1 to 30 days past due. In-house collectors now make up a large share of the staff handling these accounts up 19% from September.

Sources indicate that that helped us take a more active role in managing early delinquency. And second, we are expanding our use of AI in post loan management. We were already using AI for early-stage collections. Now we are also using it for accounts that have been overdue for longer. For those accounts, the monthly recovery rate with AI is almost 1.5x the rate third-party collection agencies achieved through phone calls. That reveals how AI can help improve collections efficiency. So take them together, these changes have strengthened our collection capacities and helped improve the recoveries. That helped during our 30-day collection rate a bit in October. That is the improvement is still recent.

According to recent reports, it's still too early to call a turning point in credit risk, and we will need a bit more time to see where the improvement holds. So looking ahead, we expect risk to ease gradually and higher risk loans for early vintage result and as the mix of fresh loans continue to improve. The pace of recovery will still depend on the external environment. Yes, that's the key. We will keep a close eye on the risk indicators and adjust our origination volume accordingly with asset quality and profitability as our top priority.

Operator: Our next question will come from the line of from Jing China International Capital Corporation.

In a recent development, yujie Jing: [Foreign Language] I'm Yujie Jing from CICC. And I have 2 questions. First, on capital allocation, given the changing domestic operating environment and ongoing funding needs for overseas expansion, how does management think about the overall capital allocation framework? And what are your key considerations in balancing business growth, financial prudence, and shareholder returns? Secondly, turning to overseas business. It has been 1 year since the acquisition of Fundo in Q4 last year. Could you walk us through the key progress of the Australia business over this period? And what will be the priority investment areas in 2027? Also, what is the management's framework for evaluating and entering other development markets going forward?

In a recent development, jiayuan Xu: I will take your first one. We have always been prudent about how we use our capital while keeping enough flexibility to adjust as conditions change. We will look at what the business needs, how much liquidity we should keep on hand and how much capital we can return to shareholders. First, the funding business remains our top priority. For China business, we are still seeing some pressure on the funding side and on the credit side. So we need enough liquidity to respond as market conditions change. And at the same time, our overseas business continues to grow. So we need to fund that growth in Indonesia, the Philippines, and Australia.

With both needs in mind, we will keep a healthy cash position. That helps us in 2 ways: First, our strong liquidity position gives us our institution funding partners confidence in us and supports our relationships; Second, when market shift, we can draw our cash reserves to respond promptly and keep the business running smoothly. At the end of Q3, we had around USD 1.2 billion in cash and short-term investments. That puts us in a strong financial position and gives us flexibility in how we use our capital. And on the debt side, we are also looking for opportunity to manage our debt where market conditions are favorable.

As we have mentioned in October, we bought back a portion of our outstanding CB that reduced the long-term debt we will need to repay and the interest will pay overtime and it give us more financial flexibility. Second, we have provided for the needs of business and keep sufficient liquidity on hand. We look at shareholders' return. Our buyback, we keep the pace flexible based on where our shares are trading, market liquidity, our cash position, and our overall capital need. In the first 9 months of the year, we bought back USD 71.1 million worth of shares. And at the end of Q3, our shares outstanding were down 5.8% from the end of last year.

We also continue to see dividends as an key way to return capital to shareholders. So looking ahead, we will keep reviewing this prioritize as our business [ interact ], their funding needs evolve and the market conditions change, our goal is to support the long-term growth while continuing to create value for our shareholders. So that's for the first question, and Tim will take the second one.

Tiezheng Li: I will answer the question about our Australia business. So let me cover 3 things, the results, what we did, and what's next. First, the results. Australia is our first developed market and Fundo was our first time entering account market through acquisition. By year-end, the numbers are quite good. In Q3, upcoming borrowers more than doubled year-over-year. Transaction volume grew nearly 80% and loan balance doubled. Revenue was up about 50% and the profitability improved a lot as well. For a mature credit market, that's broadly in line with what we expected when we did the deal. And second, what's behind those numbers, there are 4 things.

One, compliance: Australia sets a high bar on consumer protection and how lenders assess a borrower's ability to repay. We invest heavily here. We improved how we assess income, revenue expenses, and the existing debt. And in June, we connected to open banking. So with the customer consent, we can see their banking transaction data directly. That makes our assessment more accurate to technology. Fundo used to serve customers mainly through its website. We debuted our own app in Q4 last year, and it's now 40% of our origination. Customers on the app stay longer and follow again more often. Three, the team. Fundo's original team is stable. Retention is about 90% and everyone in the payroll has stayed.

They know the local market and the regulations. We brought in our risk models, and product experience, and operating know-how. The 2 sides complement each other well. And four, the product mix. When we bought Fundo, most loans were small and short term. By Q3, medium and large loans were 51% of the mix, up from 38% a year ago. That means we are serving better quality borrowers with higher limits and longer terms. And third, what's next? In 2027, we will keep investing in Australia on products, more of the larger, longer-term loans on operations, a better app experience, lower acquisition costs, and higher retention. So that growth turns into sustained profit.

Sources indicate that and longer term, Australia matters beyond its own revenue and profit. Customers here borrow more and have a higher lifetime value than in developing markets. We've learned to operate under higher regulated standard, and we will show that our models work, buy a local platform, keep the core team, and bringing the group's technology and operations. We want to take that experience to other mature markets over time. So scale in developing markets, customer value in mature markets. That gives us more diversified global portfolio.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to hand the call back to the company for closing.

Yam Cheng: Thank you, Desmond. Thank you once again for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please feel free to contact us in the future. Thank you.

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s said they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV reveals on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

Industry observers note that perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

It’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

It has been revealed that the Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

According to recent reports, some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

Sources indicate that the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

According to recent reports, for most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

In a recent development, the Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Industry observers note that unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

Industry observers note that proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

Recent findings suggest that an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

It has been revealed that if that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to enhancement all your other accounts.

It’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

It has been revealed that when you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an notable document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

It has been revealed that pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

Industry observers note that proton Unlimited bundles Pass with Proton VPN, Proton Mail, Proton Drive, and more, including 500 GB of cloud storage. It’s the option to consider if you also want a VPN, encrypted email, and cloud storage alongside your password manager.

A password manager isn’t the most conspicuous Black Friday purchase, but it’s one you can put to work immediately: the next account you create, the next password you forget, or the next time a checkout asks for details you don’t have handy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • In a recent development, the new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the newly introduced Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

In a recent development, the new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app owners on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

Sources indicate that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

In a recent development, agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

Sources indicate that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of upcoming tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google declared AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (602 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.
  • Industry observers note that the partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles.
  • In a recent development, now, the partnership is ready to take its next substantial step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.

Industry observers note that the partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

In a recent development, now, the partnership is ready to take its next substantial step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies noted. They plan to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber plans to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

Industry observers note that “Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an important milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

Nuro says it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

In May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the company the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

Sources indicate that the Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

According to recent reports, it’s been a substantial year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has rolled out investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple has quietly announced the upcoming opening of its latest retail store in Hyderabad, India. Located at the Lakeshore Mall in Kukatpally, it opens at 5pm on Thursday, December 10.

As is now usual, the manufacturer has created some exclusive wallpaper to mark the event, and you can download it for iPhone, iPad, and Mac ….

Sources indicate that the store will be the seventh one to open in India. There’s no press release or photos as yet – the organization has simply quietly added the store to its list in the country.

In a recent development, as we’ve previously explained, Apple had been trying to open retail stores in India since at least 2015, but had to undertake a lengthy battle with the government before finally being allowed to do so in 2023. Since then, the tech giant has averaged two newly introduced stores a year.

According to recent reports, india has taken a clever approach to economic development, offering both incentives to establish local manufacturing plants, and barriers to imports of foreign-made products. That carrot-and-stick approach has proven successful, with companies like Apple jumping through the necessary hoops in order to sell their products to the second largest population in the world.

In a recent development, an India First initiative required companies to manufacture a significant proportion of their products within the country in order to avoid high import tariffs. This forced Apple, Samsung, and other companies to establish manufacturing plants in India, bringing jobs to the country.

Additionally, India does not allow company-branded retail stores unless the same conditions are met. That particular requirement was mostly intended to target Apple.

The proposal worked, with Apple asking its suppliers and iPhone assemblers to establish manufacturing plants within India. Initially, that was just for the iPhone SE, but more advanced phones have gradually been added, and today the country is the second largest manufacturing base after China. All iPhones sold in the US are made in India.

Apple has for some time now created unique wallpapers to mark the opening of each fresh store, and the latest example is particularly beautiful.

According to recent reports, to download it, you need to visit this page on the device for which you want to use it. For example, if you visit the page on a Mac, you will automatically be taken to the desktop version.

According to the Monthly Indicator of Economic Activity, MIEA, (sic) [ Monthly Estimator of Economic Activity, EMAE, ] the Argentine economy contracted 1.2% year-over-year in September, while edging up 1.1% month-over-month on a seasonally adjusted basis. Activity levels stood 2.4% below those recorded in December 2025. As of September 2026, the primary fiscal surplus reached 1.2% of GDP with total revenues declining 4.3% year-over-year in real terms and primary spending falling 2.3%. At the same time, inflation continued to moderate.

Sources indicate that consumer prices increased 5.8% during the quarter compared with 6.8% in the second quarter. This was positive for purchasing power, planning and the long-term development of financial intermediation. In the short term, however, it also accelerated the decline in nominal interest rates and reduced the returns generated by CPI-linked assets. During the last 12 months, inflation reached 33.4% in September. The monetary base increased 0.9% in real terms during the third quarter and declined 16.4% in real terms compared with September 2025. The average exchange rate of the quarter was ARS 1,500 per dollar. And at the end of the quarter, the exchange rate reached ARS 1,517 per dollar, representing a 7.6% year-over-year depreciation.

Dollar deposits remained dynamic, while in pesos, we see the transactional deposits declined year-over-year and time deposits gained share during the period. In terms of credit, the system data reflected the transition process of the macro. Real peso credit remained soft, while dollar lending continued to expand at a faster pace. In other words, the financial system moved toward a lower inflation environment, but the volume recovery was still uneven, with the volume of dollar intermediation becoming more relevant. Taken together, these trends frame our quarter. Lower inflation reduced the loss from the net monetary position, but asset yields declined faster than funding costs and volume growth is still lagging.

In a recent development, as a result, margins compressed before loan demand and transactional activity had fully recovered. Against this backdrop, Grupo Galicia generated net income of ARS 229 billion in the third quarter with an annualized ROE of 9.3% and an ROA of 1.7%. The result was 16% below the previous quarter, but represented a significant recovery from the loss recorded 1 year earlier. More importantly, profitability remained diversified. Banco Galicia contributed with ARS 134.9 billion, Galicia Asset Management with ARS 48.5 billion, Naranja X with ARS 29.3 billion, Galicia Seguros with ARS 11.4 billion and Galicia Securities with ARS 5.3 billion. This diversification is strategically relevant as it helps to stabilize the group's earnings capacity.

Industry observers note that for the first 9 months of 2026, net income reached ARS 577.5 billion with an 8% ROE. The performance indicates that the group has moved beyond the losses recorded in 2025 and is rebuilding profitability on a more sustainable operating base. The decline in profitability from the second quarter was largely explained by the reduction in the group's financial margin, which fell to 14.4% as lower lending rates, lower CPI returns and fewer gains from security sales affected revenues. But this should be read together with positive developments. The cost of risk kept on decreasing from the peak recorded in December last year and expenses declined materially year-over-year, improving the efficiency ratio more than 20 percentage points.

Industry observers note that banco Galicia, our largest subsidiary, is where the change in the earnings environment was most visible. Net income reached ARS 134.9 billion with a 7% ROE. The 19% sequential decline in profitability was primarily a consequence of margin compression, partially offset by the improvement in most of the lines related to expenses, in which our focus in efficiencies is showing results. During the quarter, average interest-earning assets increased 2% to ARS 32 trillion, but their average yield declined to 22.3% from 27.1%. Average interest-bearing liabilities increased 1%, while their cost fell to 9% from 10.1%.

Funding costs moved in the right direction, but not as promptly as asset yields, which explains a significant part of the reduction in net interest income. Within the asset mix by currency, average peso loans grew 3%, foreign currency loans increased 9% and peso government securities declined 6%. This was a quarter of selective allocation with the bank reducing public sector exposure and prioritizing lending opportunities with an appropriate risk-adjusted return. Going to our interest-bearing liabilities, in the chart on the right, we can see the volume of those denominated in foreign currency, which increased by 6%. And on the left, that in pesos, they decreased 4%.

According to recent reports, interest income reached ARS 1.7 trillion, declining 12% sequentially and 24% year-over-year as lending rates and CPI returns fell. Interest expenses reached ARS 586 billion, also decreasing quarter-over-quarter. When we compare the figures with the ones of the third quarter of the previous year, the reduction was significant, mainly due to the increase in the cost of funding associated to the volatility of the midterm elections that took place last year. Fee income amounted to ARS 317 billion and decreased 3% in real terms in the third quarter, with most of the sources of fees behaving similarly, while results from financial instruments returned to more normalized levels after the strong gains recorded in the second quarter.

Sources indicate that FX results amounted to ARS 119 billion and increased 3% in the quarter, mainly due to the trading activity with our clients. The most encouraging development of the quarter was the change in credit trends. Loan loss provisions declined 12% sequentially to ARS 509 billion. The NPL ratio improved to 7.8% from 8.3%. Cost of risk fell to 8% from 9.3% and coverage increased to 96.1% from 92.8%. Fewer exposures migrated to Stage 3, deterioration in the retail portfolio slowed and nonaccrual financing declined. This suggests that the credit cycle began to stabilize during the quarter. We remain cautious as NPL levels are still above those recorded 1 year ago and improvement must be sustained over several quarters.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the direction of the trend is now positive. The actions taken in underwriting, collections, portfolio management and provisioning are beginning to translate into better asset quality metrics. This is crucial for the earnings outlook. As the cost of risk normalizes, a larger portion of operating income can translate into bottom line profitability even in a lower rate environment. The second major structural message is efficiency. Banco Galicia's expenses declined 10% quarter-over-quarter and 36% year-over-year to ARS 731 billion. Personnel expenses fell 15% sequentially. Administrative expenses declined 5% and other operating expenses were 10% lower. These reductions reflect the efficiency initiatives implemented throughout the year and the benefits of the integration with HSBC Argentina.

It has been revealed that lower maintenance, IT, communications and administrative service costs demonstrate that the combined platform is beginning to operate with greater scale. The group's efficiency ratio was 39.4%. It increased sequentially because revenues compressed faster than expenses, but it improved by more than 20 percentage points compared with the third quarter of the previous year. Our objective is to continue simplifying the operating model while protecting customer experience, digital capabilities and the capacity to grow. Financing to the private sector totaled ARS 26 trillion and declined 3% sequentially, reflecting the softer level of demand and our selective approach to origination. Market share of financing to the private sector decreased 30 basis points to 14.7%.

Deposits were stable at ARS 28.7 trillion, while private sector deposits market share increased 20 basis points to 14.5%. Peso-denominated deposits decreased 3%, while dollar deposits increased 3%. Time deposits in pesos increased 12%, while transactional deposits in pesos decreased 11%, negatively affecting the cost of funding. Liquidity remained high. Liquid assets represented 99.7% of transactional deposits and 56.1% of total deposits. Capitalization was equally strong with a total capital ratio of 25.7% and Tier 1 ratio of 25.6%. Computable capital exceeded the regulatory minimum by ARS 4.8 trillion. This buffer provides strategic optionality. They allow us to absorb volatility, protect the franchise and accelerate growth when demand returns and risk-adjusted spreads become more attractive.

They allow the group to participate in payments, consumer finance, insurance, savings and capital markets, creating a broader and more balanced platform for growth. Galicia Asset Management delivered net income of ARS 48 billion, while assets under management reached ARS 16.6 trillion.
