📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the flood is too much for Tidal. The music streaming app unveiled on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated. The platform mentioned it’s making the move after being increasingly inundated with non-human music. As of Dec. 9, Tidal will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated tracks.

The app also remarked distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.

According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov. 6 alone. Tidal said the affected tracks were labeled as AI and removed from the royalty pool, which is the pot of subscription and ad revenue paid out to rights holders.

In a recent development, before Tuesday’s action, Tidal had tried to lessen AI’s influence by identifying, labeling and demonetizing AI tracks, as outlined in its AI policy. But amid the growing influx of AI music, representatives for the app remarked it was time for “a more drastic change.”.

Tidal said there are 27 million tracks in its catalog that are 100% AI, but 96% of them have not been streamed at all in the past three months. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of Tidal’s entire listings.

The company has removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for artist-name impersonation.

Some AI help is permitted. Musical tracks where the maker used AI assistance but did not rely on it to generate the entire track will be allowed on the platform. Tidal uses ⁠Ircam Amplify to detect AI.

A Tidal representative told CNET that the app does not set a maximum amount of AI assistance that can be used to make tracks, and affirmed that only tracks that are deemed 100% AI-generated would be removed.

It has been revealed that read more: I Only Listened to AI Music for a Week. It Was Terrible, but Not for the Reason You Think.

According to recent reports, “Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more,” the organization said in its announcement. “Everything in this enhancement comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for or copied by someone pretending to be you.”.

Generating music with AI is increasingly easy with online tools. The AI song-generation platform Suno can create songs using only text prompts. With Google’s Lyria, you can use photos or text prompts to generate tracks up to 3 minutes long.

AI music also is not just about creating hit songs. Some industries need affordable music for short-form videos, games, apps and retail spaces, and they are increasingly turning to AI to supply it.

But streaming apps and other companies are fighting back against AI slop, which refers to often poor-quality AI-generated social media posts, articles, music, videos and images inundating the internet in an attempt to generate click-and-stream revenue.

YouTube recently rolled out a upcoming labeling system to indicate which music is AI-generated. Deezer provides a free tool listeners can use to see which tracks are AI-generated. Spotify is labeling which musicians are AI and which are human. Apple is flagging AI-generated music so listeners can spot it.

Industry observers note that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two latest credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

According to recent reports, the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

Recent findings suggest that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

Recent findings suggest that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

According to recent reports, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for fresh applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

According to recent reports, elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

According to recent reports, to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

It has been revealed that wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Industry observers note that travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

It has been revealed that the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

It has been revealed that however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

In a recent development, the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

In a recent development, plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

In a recent development, those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

One of the most interesting perks of the fresh cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

Industry observers note that there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • With Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A newly introduced feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic mentioned. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

In a recent development, the upcoming feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic mentioned, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

According to recent reports, as a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic mentioned.

According to recent reports, “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic mentioned it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

In a recent development, “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz mentioned the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

In a recent development, also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

Recent findings suggest that “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he noted. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz stated he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the company and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he mentioned.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the fresh state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

It has been revealed that individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “consumers won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

It has been revealed that still, that depends on the number of PRs people are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the upcoming PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

According to recent reports, anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

High grocery prices have been in the news for years now. The cost of eggs, how much you’re paying for a bowl of cereal and whether or not meat is back on the menu are the recurring subjects of nationwide headlines.

So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.

It has been revealed that although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound. Here’s what happened when I tried to use AI agents to find the lowest possible prices on groceries.

It has been revealed that AI agents such as Meta Muse and ChatGPT’s Dots can only crawl so many sites and online fliers for prices. Some stores and e-commerce sites have blocked AI agents from accessing their URLs. The first step in finding cheaper groceries with AI agents is to check which sites and stores they can access for price comparisons.

Where both agents missed a step was in the limitations they put on their searches, at first only looking at the retailers I had shown via my receipts and a few other major-name grocery stores.

I clarified in the chats and in a 20-minute voice conversation with Muse and a 14-minute voice conversation with Dots that they should expand their horizons and look at discount online retailers like Martie.com, and check what they could around advertised pricing and offerings at local farmers’ markets.

Muse stuck to the basics like Ralphs, Target and Walmart, and then expanded to Sprouts, Vons and Martie.com when prompted.

After further nudging, Muse also reviewed user-reported pricing from Costco (I don’t have a membership), gave me vague information about Grocery Outlet, suggested Misfits Market/Imperfect Foods, ruled out Amazon Fresh and gave me some sample pricing from a local butcher for meats.

Muse also checked some local bakery prices after I mentioned I’d like to find alternatives to sweet treats at a more affordable price.

Dots checked all the usual places that Meta Muse checked with a few extras thrown in — Smart & Final for produce, meat and some packaged products, and Super King’s monthly ad.

Industry observers note that neither of the tools checked Trader Joe’s. Muse noted that the grocery chain doesn’t show prices of its products online, despite me finding that the Trader Joe’s website demonstrates prices of its products online. Both Dots and Muse admitted to only checking the local store’s pages when asked.

Industry observers note that you could spend some time making a list from scratch of all the groceries you might need every two weeks and give that list to the AI agent for its search. You could also skip all that and take some pics of your most recent grocery receipts and online payments and have the AI agent build the list itself.

Recent findings suggest that I had some receipts saved, and the AI agents I used for this test were able to put together an accurate grocery list from them. I also provided emails showing receipts from online orders of household items and groceries for the past month to build my orders.

Muse took my receipts and concluded that, surprise, surprise, shopping at Gelson’s was not as cost-effective as shopping at Walmart. It spat out a lot of specific information about comparisons on some of the items in my list, but completely ignored others.

Dots looked over my receipts and recommended I try shopping at Super King for most fresh meat, produce and a few grains, and keep Walmart as my main option for packaged products like pasta sauce.

Both tools tackled this task in a way I was not expecting — as a narrative exploration of my overall grocery spending, with generalized suggestions supported by specific examples of spot pricing.

It was kind of like they’ve been optimized to write essays about grocery shopping as a school assignment, and not to be agentic personal assistants for real-world work.

Maybe it was the way I phrased the task, but I was hoping to get an actual shopping list with price comparisons for each item, or at least equivalent items, and a guide on where and how to procure said items.

Neither AI agent provided this autonomously and had to be directly prompted to provide grocery lists in response to a very specific request.

Industry observers note that AI agents are supposed to be pros at anticipating the needs of their human bosses. I was keen to see how the always-on AI agents would handle managing the recurring needs of a small household and if they might make any autonomous suggestions meant to save me money in ways I hadn’t anticipated.

At no point did Muse seem to be actually thinking outside the strict parameters of the review of the items on the receipts I sent. This felt more like a conversation about what I’d previously purchased with a side serving of attempts to get me to connect Instacart to the tool.

It was also the most confusing grocery shopping experience I have ever had. That might be on me, but I would assume the agent might ask some questions, like how often I usually shop, what my monthly budget for groceries is, and how many people and animals live in the house. Muse didn’t ask any of those things and had to be prompted consistently.

Muse sent me the final grocery list as a raw Markdown file, which was hilarious. I got a .pdf version after explicitly asking for one.

My original total with one in-person shop and one online order was about $180. Muse’s total with three in-person shops and one online order came in at around $153.

Dots was slightly better suited to this task after some prodding, and gave me some options for building prep meals with low-effort, high-protein recipes based on how I usually shop.

Dots’ final grocery list included everything I asked for, but still missed some key items, like solid substitutes for pricey prepped foods. Dot’s final total with two in-person shopping trips and a whole lot of missing items came out to around $85.

Industry observers note that this test reinforced my findings about how agentic AI tools tackle domestic or traditionally invisible labor tasks. In my limited use cases so far, they are about as useful as a loose dog turd tumbling around in a clothes dryer.

If you’re not looking to book a flight and hotel for a business conference in Philadelphia or put your Sweetgreen order on autopilot, the AI agents exhibit a startling lack of curiosity and autonomous thinking.

Sources indicate that there’s still a large gap in common sense on the part of agentic AI for those of us hoping these tools will make our everyday lives outside of a 9-to-5 easier, more affordable or less hectic. I hope that changes as they learn.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Todd Shriber – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than iShares Bitcoin Trust ›.

It is Form 13F filing season, meaning it's a good time to bone up on exactly what that regulatory document is. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) requires that investors exercising "investment discretion over $100 million or more" reveal their holdings in Form 13F within 45 days of the end of the prior quarter.

According to recent reports, likely due in part to some investors' reverence for Warren Buffett, among other famous professional market participants, following 13F filings is something of a sport. However, it's not always the best way to track what the smart money is doing.

Sources indicate that wells Fargo increased its holdings of the iShares Bitcoin Trust, but that’s not a buy signal. Image source: Getty Images.

Take the case of Wells Fargo (WFC -0.31%) and the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT +0.92%), the largest spot Bitcoin (BTC +4.19%) exchange-traded fund (ETF).

Third-quarter 13F filings indicate that several banks, including Wells Fargo, increased exposure to various spot Bitcoin ETFs. On the surface, that may be all some investors need to know before grabbing for the falling knife (hopefully a temporary condition) that is the world's largest cryptocurrency.

It has been revealed that indeed, Wells Fargo more than doubled its holdings of the iShares Bitcoin Trust to nearly 49.6 million, worth about $2.4 billion, as of the end of the third quarter. Investors need to dig deeper than that. Here's why: roughly 85% of the bank's position in the king of Bitcoin ETFs is held on behalf of brokerage clients.

It has been revealed that put another way, the bulk of Wells Fargo's stake in the Bitcoin ETF is attributable to folks who trade on the bank's platform or to clients of Wells Fargo Advisors – the bank's wealth management arm. That means that the bank, for the most part, is NOT directly making a directional bet on the iShares ETFs. It's merely taking custody of the fund on behalf of its customers who own it.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, wells Fargo's involvement with the Bitcoin ETF isn't comparable to, say, Berkshire Hathaway revealing a new position or adding to an existing holding. News to that effect often boosts the stock in question because Berkshire is making a clear bullish bet. That's simply not the case with Wells Fargo and this Bitcoin ETF.

Bitcoin bulls  (sometimes known in crypto lingo as HODLers) who are disappointed by the revelation that Wells Fargo's substantial boost to its Bitcoin ETF position means little can take heart, as there are some encouraging signs in other 13Fs. For example, Wall Street firms added $4.2 billion in Bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, and institutional holdings of those ETFs hit a record in the July-September period.

Importantly, some of those professional investors are using Bitcoin ETFs to make directional bets. Plus, data confirm that some well-known hedge fund managers either added to or initiated positions in the iShares ETF in the third quarter.

Still, caution is warranted because some recent buyers of Bitcoin ETFs may have already ditched those positions, and the investing public won't know that until fourth-quarter 13Fs come out next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:41AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Sandisk ›.

Sandisk (SNDK -5.57%) expects revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion this quarter, up from $11.0 billion last quarter. But as of the Nov. 20 close, the stock stood around 73% below its split-adjusted record close from June 25.

Sandisk isn't alone. Western Digital (WDC -0.55%) closed that day 65% under the record it reached on June 18, and Seagate Technology (STX -2.10%) finished 58% below its June 22 peak. SK Hynix (SKHY -0.75%) ended the day 48% below its Sept. 9 closing high, its lowest close since its July debut on the Nasdaq. All four rebounded sharply on Nov. 23, but each was still more than 30% below its peak.

In a recent development, put another way, investors look to be pricing in the end of this memory and storage boom. But I think the sell-off has gone too far, given what these four companies are reporting.

Showing how much cash the flash memory maker now pulls in, Sandisk produced $6.3 billion of free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) in the three months through Oct. 2, its fiscal first quarter of 2027. That compares to $438 million a year before.

In a recent development, even after $5.0 billion of buybacks, Sandisk closed the quarter with $5.1 billion of cash. It has no debt. And that one quarter of free cash flow is around 6% of the organization's market value of about $105 billion.

Industry observers note that growth is slowing, of course, from 23% sequentially in fiscal Q1 to about 12% at the midpoint of this quarter's guidance. But the midpoint of management's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings guidance comes to around $7 per share after the 8-for-1 stock split. Multiply that by four, and the stock trades for only about 3 times earnings. That price arguably assumes most of today's profits vanish within a few years.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, earlier this month, I estimated Western Digital stock could be worth around $500 by 2030 -- returns of about 8% a year from the $366 or so it traded at then. At about $300 as I write, the same $500 would mean returns of about 13% yearly, not counting dividends.

Recent findings suggest that the hard drive maker's adjusted earnings per share rose from $1.78 a year before to $3.56 in fiscal Q4 2026 and $4.64 in fiscal Q1 2027. Not only does management expect $5.80 in fiscal Q2 at the midpoint of its guidance, but it also expects revenue growth of 66% to 72% year over year, a rise from the 55% it just posted. That puts the stock at around 13 times annualized guided earnings.

It has been revealed that my estimate hasn't moved, but the price has. At this level, I think Western Digital shares are a buy.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Seagate has used its jump in profits to pay down debt swiftly. Its gross debt was around $3.6 billion on July 3. After retiring around $1.2 billion in its fiscal first quarter of 2027 and another $750 million after the quarter closed, it's down to $1.6 billion. Seagate had $1.3 billion in cash on Oct. 2, before the latest repayment.

Also, Seagate's adjusted earnings per share almost tripled year over year to $7.68 in fiscal Q1. Management expects $9.20 in fiscal Q2.

At around $520, shares trade at about 14 times annualized guided earnings. That looks modest to me.

According to recent reports, SK Hynix's third-quarter revenue grew 32% from the second quarter and 328% year over year, to around 104.6 trillion won. Operating profit soared 632% year over year to around 83.3 trillion won, an operating margin of about 80%.

Better yet, the South Korean chipmaker finished the quarter with 114.5 trillion won in cash and cash equivalents versus 15.8 trillion won in borrowings, for net cash of 98.7 trillion won. It also plans around 100 trillion won of shareholder returns for 2026.

Still, on expected 2027 earnings, SK Hynix's price-to-earnings ratio is only about 3. At that price, the market arguably expects profits to drop steeply long before 2030.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Recent findings suggest that over a decade, I'd expect at least one memory bust. Flash memory, DRAM, and hard drive prices can all drop sharply when supply catches up, and these stocks could fall more before they recover.

#199871. What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

Recent findings suggest that an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

Sources indicate that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

In a recent development, inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

According to recent reports, detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

It has been revealed that however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Sources indicate that some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

Sources indicate that car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several customers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

Once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response said, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

In a recent development, when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to New York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

While Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

It has been revealed that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

“Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” said Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

Around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

It’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

“We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster noted.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind.
  • It has been revealed that “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.

SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040.

It has been revealed that “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite releases, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.”.

Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the company’s IPO in June.

Recent findings suggest that “You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk noted in March.

On its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It says that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation.

Space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow.

It’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years?

“We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.”.

SpaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that introduced last year in total.

Sources indicate that scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center strategy would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year.

“There are scientific papers out there raising concerns,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?”.

The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society.

A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

What Are Repositioning Cruises?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

Sources indicate that one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

Industry observers note that just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit crucial sites when off the ship.

Sources indicate that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy demonstrates, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

Industry observers note that if Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. How to Prepare for RMDs Starting at 75 — Even If You're Only 60 Right Now

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, fifteen years might seem like a long way in the future.
  • Recent findings suggest that required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) may feel like a problem to deal with later if you're 60 years old.
  • Here are four specific actions a 60-year-old can take right now to meaningfully reduce the RMD burden at 75.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keith Speights – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:44AM EST.

In a recent development, fifteen years might seem like a long way in the future. However, time goes by swiftly.

Recent findings suggest that required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) may feel like a problem to deal with later if you're 60 years old. After all, for anyone born in 1960 or later, the tax obligation doesn't start until age 75. But that instinct is precisely what makes RMDs the most expensive retirement-planning mistake people make. The decisions available at 60 are worth far more than any RMD strategy available at 74 -- and by the time most people start thinking about this, the best options have already closed.

Here are four specific actions a 60-year-old can take right now to meaningfully reduce the RMD burden at 75.

1. Run the projection now, not at 74.

It has been revealed that the first step is understanding what your RMD will actually be. The IRS calculates RMDs by dividing the prior year-end account balance by a life expectancy factor from the Uniform Lifetime Table -- approximately 24.6 for a 75-year-old. A 60-year-old with $500,000 in a traditional IRA today, growing at 7% annually, will have around $1.29 million by the end of the year they turn 74, implying a first-year RMD of roughly $52,400. Running that projection now creates the awareness that motivates everything else on this list.

Industry observers note that 2. Begin Roth conversions in the low-tax window.

In a recent development, the years between 60 and 74 -- particularly before Social Security begins and before RMDs start -- are typically the lowest-tax period of a retiree's financial life. Converting traditional IRA funds to Roth IRAs during this window pays today's tax rate on the converted amount in exchange for permanently removing that balance from future RMD calculations. Even modest annual conversions of $20,000 to $50,000 over 15 years can meaningfully shrink the RMD burden at 75. Importantly, Roth IRAs have no RMDs at all during the original owner's lifetime.

3. Coordinate conversions with claiming Social Security.

The interaction between Roth conversions and Social Security taxation is the most underappreciated element of pre-RMD planning. Converting aggressively before Social Security begins keeps provisional income below the thresholds that trigger taxation on up to 85% of benefits. This can save thousands of dollars annually throughout retirement. The window for this strategy is finite and closes the moment both Social Security and RMDs begin arriving simultaneously.

4. Consider a qualified longevity annuity contract.

Sources indicate that the SECURE 2.0 Act allows retirees to use up to $210,000 (in 2026) of IRA funds to purchase a qualified longevity annuity contract (QLAC) -- a deferred income annuity that begins payments at a future date, typically 80 or 85. The limit is adjusted for inflation over time. Funds used for a QLAC are excluded from RMD calculations until the annuity begins paying, effectively reducing the RMD base and deferring both the income and the tax.

Age 60 isn't too soon to prepare.

It has been revealed that the most expensive RMD is the one that arrives as a surprise at 75 from an IRA that was never touched between 60 and 74. The least expensive one is the result of 15 years of quiet, deliberate preparation -- Roth conversions in low-tax years, careful Social Security coordination, and a QLAC that removes a portion of the IRA balance from the RMD calculation entirely.

Industry observers note that the problem doesn't feel urgent at 60. That's exactly why starting now produces such dramatically better outcomes than waiting until it does.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news. One of the best free options for organizing your work and home life is reaching the end of its life. Microsoft plans to retire its To Do app at the end of June 2027.

We’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired. But several Microsoft-watching websites this week spotted a blog post from the firm recommending users switch to its Planner app.

Microsoft To Do is retiring. For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.

Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027. This includes To Do on the web, Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android, for both work or school accounts and personal Microsoft accounts.

Industry observers note that the underlying To Do service, APIs, and related synchronization support will retire on separate, later timelines. We’ll communicate those dates and any required preparation separately.

In a recent development, but there’s a big catch for Microsoft customers who are on 365 Personal or 365 Family plans: Planner will not be available to them. That means Microsoft is telling To Do people on those accounts to find a comparable app elsewhere if they’re not on a business account that includes Planner.

The change was also mentioned in a separate Microsoft post about unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365 from Microsoft product manager Ashna Patel.

According to recent reports, in a statement provided to CNET, Howard Crow, director of product, agents and AI at Microsoft, said the change consolidates task management across Microsoft 365. “We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare,” Crow said.

Crow mentioned the firm will share more information about the transition in the coming months.

While the end of June 2027 may sound like a very long time from now, the path Microsoft has offered for To Do people is not a great one if you want to take action now. There’s no built-in export feature in the app, though in the blog post, Microsoft promises, “Microsoft will provide a way to export your To Do data before the apps retire. We’ll revision this article with instructions, supported data, requirements, and limitations when those details are finalized.”.

Already, there are some pretty severe limitations even for those on Microsoft prepares that support Planner: Existing To Do list items won’t work after that June deadline. “After that date, you will no longer be able to view or manage them in Planner,” the post stated.

In the meantime, you can shop around for alternate apps, some free, including Google Keep, ToDoist and Notion.

Recent findings suggest that to Do consumers, myself included, are not happy. As Windows Latest reported, comments in response to Microsoft’s decision included, “Do you actually hate your users?”.

If this were simply a case of Microsoft creating software people didn’t like and then abandoning it, that would be one thing. But the To Do retirement is especially painful for those of us who were forced to move to Microsoft’s app a few years after it purchased Wunderlist.

Wunderlist was a German app that launched in 2011 and quickly became popular for its slick interface, easy-to-patch task lists and its availability across web, desktop and mobile platforms. Microsoft absorbed some of Wunderlist into To Do and killed the original app in 2020 without ever offering all of the features that made Wunderlist great.

As someone who used Wunderlist for years and has been using To Do, I can tell you that while To Do has been essential in my work and personal life, it never became as intuitive to use as Wunderlist. It never handled predictive task creation as well as Wunderlist did (such as understanding as you typed the date of a task or if it was repeating). It lacked features for sharing lists or collaborating on them, and simply didn’t look as stylish. As far as aesthetics, the best thing Microsoft did with To Do was add a Dark Mode.

Industry observers note that wunderlist was a joy to use. To Do always felt like the knockoff diet version of it and never quite as good.

After several years, I simply gave up on the idea that Microsoft would improve the app or add any new features, but kept using it out of necessity given the lack of a built-in export option.

Sources indicate that the death announcement is not surprising. Just sad.

RIP To Do, but really RIP to the last remnants of Wunderlist.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks users do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

“When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic said.

In a recent development, artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they revision automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free customers.

Anthropic stated the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

Sources indicate that also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

The update clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

“If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic noted.

Recent findings suggest that claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

First, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid prepares, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

Full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic stated, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and enhancement the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

“Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the organization said.

For Claude Enterprise intends, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

10 stocks we like better than Shiba Inu ›.

The Shiba Inu (SHIB +5.74%) cryptocurrency was created in 2020 by an anonymous developer named Ryoshi, who saw the success of Dogecoin and wanted to build a more useful alternative. Shiba Inu runs on the Ethereum (ETH +2.68%) network, so it inherits all of the functionality, security, and infrastructure of the world's biggest platform for developing decentralized software applications.

Sources indicate that shiba Inu soared by a whopping 45,278,000% in 2021, a return so strong that it could have turned a perfectly-timed investment of $3 into over $1 million. It's one of the largest single-year gains in the history of the financial markets, so it's no surprise many investors still watch this token.

However, speculation was the primary driver of the 2021 rally, so it simply wasn't sustainable. Shiba Inu has since lost 96% of its peak value, and trades at just $0.0000036 per token as I write this on Nov. 24. But there is one way Shiba Inu could stage another historic bull run, and potentially even reach $1 per token. Can it happen in 2027? The answer might shock you.

Having a legitimate source of demand is the key to sustainable upside for any asset. People buy real estate because houses have utility, and they buy stocks because the underlying companies generate revenue and earnings. Many cryptocurrencies also have real use-cases that attract demand, although whether it will last over the long term is up for debate.

XRP (XRP +4.84%), for example, is the native cryptocurrency in Ripple's payment network. It helps banks send money around the world instantly, and with minimal fees. Then there is Ether, the native coin in the Ethereum network, which is used to pay fees that cover the computing costs when people use decentralized software applications.

Sources indicate that since Shiba Inu is built on Ethereum, users can program smart contracts to establish autonomous rules when using the token on decentralized platforms like lending marketplaces and crypto exchanges. Developers created a Layer-2 blockchain solution called Shibarium to improve transaction speeds and reduce costs, but it hasn't necessarily made the Shiba Inu ecosystem any more popular.

Industry observers note that unlike Ether, Shiba Inu isn't required to build decentralized apps or cover the associated fees. Plus, while it can technically be used as a payment mechanism, just 1,254 businesses around the world are willing to accept it in exchange for goods and services (according to Cryptwerk).

Sources indicate that in short, Shiba Inu continues to lack a true use case, and the subsequent lack of organic demand is the main reason it has lost 96% of its peak value. However, there's an even bigger glitch standing in the way of a meaningful recovery.

CRYPTO · As of 11:00 AM ET 11/26/26.

Industry observers note that shiba Inu has a circulating supply of 589.2 trillion tokens, so at the current price of $0.0000036 per token, it has a market capitalization of $2.15 billion. Therefore, basic math suggests that a price of $1 per token would result in a market cap of $589.2 trillion, which would make Shiba Inu almost nine times as valuable as all 500 companies in the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) combined.

In a recent development, such a high valuation is impossible to justify, so there is no way Shiba Inu will reach $1 as things presently stand. However, the community is trying to resolve the supply problem by "burning" tokens, which typically involves sending them to a dead wallet where they can never be retrieved. In theory, the price per token should increase in proportion to the number of tokens taken out of circulation, creating a real potential pathway to the $1 milestone.

Based on Shiba Inu's market cap of $2.15 billion, burning 99.99998% of the 589.2 trillion tokens presently in supply could result in a price of $1 per token.

However, only 349 million tokens were burned in October, which equates to an annualized rate of 4.2 billion. It would take an eye-popping 140,285 years to burn enough supply to justify a price of $1 per token at this pace, so it definitely won't happen in 2027.

In a recent development, but there is even more bad news. Burning tokens doesn't create any real value, so nobody will make any money. Every investor would simply have 99.99998% fewer tokens, so even though each token would be worth $1, their net financial position won't have changed.

Well, actually, 140,000 years' worth of inflation would make the descendents of each investor significantly worse off.

We Shot a Ship Into an Asteroid to See if It Would Move. See the First Images of the Impact

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five years ago, NASA introduced its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed.
  • Industry observers note that the ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere.
  • At the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five years ago, NASA introduced its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed. The mission was a success, making Dimorphos the first celestial object whose orbit was moved by humans. And now, the European Space Agency has published images showing the damage the mission caused to the asteroid.

Industry observers note that the ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere. The images shown during the livestream were captured by the ESA’s Hera, which was rolled out in October 2024 and spent two years in deep space with its two CubeSats to measure, map, probe and eventually land on the asteroid.

At the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth. But they were unable to get a good enough view to see how much damage it did to the asteroid or any other potential changes that occurred.

This means that researchers had to estimate the damage until Hera highlighted scientists exactly what happened. Spoiler: All of those estimates were incorrect, and by a wide margin.

Sources indicate that hera indicated the damage was vastly more significant than originally thought. Scientists believed the impact would generate a 20-meter crater; Hera found that almost the entire end of the asteroid had been blown off, resulting in a crater the size of a football stadium and as wide as Dimorphos itself. This is visible in the above image — as you can see, Dimorphos used to be roughly the shape of an egg. Now, it’s the shape of a deviled egg or a kidney bean, depending on which angle you view it from.

The ESA’s Hera team discovered another neat effect of the impact: Before DART crashed into the asteroid, it was tidally locked to Didymos, much like the moon is to Earth. Scientists expected it to stay that way after the impact, but the images from Hera confirmed that Dimorphos now tumbles randomly, which none of the researchers had on their bingo card.

Recent findings suggest that “Before the DART impact, Dimorphos has always shown its same face to Didymos,” mentioned ESA Hera Mission Specialist Michael Kueppers during the presentation. “And this is what we see now. You can see it looks for a few seconds in the video like regular rotation, but it’s spinning around completely crazy.”.

ESA mission manager Ian Carnelli mentioned this surprise was great news because it’ll allow Hera to view Dimorphos on all of its sides, which would have been challenging if it were still tidally locked to Didymos.

It has been revealed that the ESA concluded the stream with one final surprise. According to Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, the Hera team told engineers that it was entirely safe to go to Dimorphos because all the debris would be ejected from the DART impact, with the remaining bits reabsorbed by Didymos and Dimorphos before Hera arrived.

According to recent reports, but there is actually quite a lot of debris around the two asteroids. Kueppers indicates they’ve identified over 100 boulders so far, marked as white dots in the image above. Despite being completely wrong about the debris field, the Hera team was in good spirits since this means there are more things for the team to study.

It has been revealed that kueppers indicates scientists are “always happy” either way because when they predict something correctly, they get awarded, and when they predict something wrong, they have a challenge to solve. “The problem is for the engineers,” he remarked.

The three discoveries were made just 20 days into Hera’s mission, which is slated to last six months. The Hera team said more images and discoveries are coming in the next half year.

The point of the DART mission was to see whether humans could deal with a potentially dangerous asteroid by ramming into it or destroying it, as is often seen in Hollywood films like Deep Impact and Armageddon. NASA even frames it as a “planetary defense test.”.

The mission was considered an overwhelming success. NASA was hoping to shorten the orbit of Dimorphos by at least 73 seconds, with the most optimal guess being approximately 10 minutes. The orbit was shortened by 33 minutes and 15 seconds. It was such a large discrepancy that scientists studied it and determined that the large amount of debris created extra recoil that amplified the push.

Recent findings suggest that the change in orbit around Didymos also changed the orbit of both asteroids around the sun by about 11.7 microns per second. This doesn’t seem significant, but it adds up to about 1 kilometer every 2.7 years. This is enough to steer potential city-killer asteroids away from Earth’s orbit, given enough time and a major enough battering ram.

Hera’s findings also show the impact was much more devastating than scientists first thought. This provides even more data for NASA and the ESA to work through to proposal for such an event if it ever happens.

“As latest data come in each day, astronomers will be able to better assess whether, and how, a mission like DART could be used in the future to help protect Earth from a collision with an asteroid if we ever discover one headed our way,” noted Lori Glaze, director of NASA’s Planetary Science Division, in a statement from 2022.

This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

The amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

Sources indicate that my point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

According to recent reports, here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

Strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI demonstrated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

In a recent development, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Markets are currently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.
